operations.specification: This operation registers a new customer account on the shopping-mall platform. The customer must provide a unique email, strong password, full name, and primary phone number. The system will validate these inputs against the 'shopping_customers' schema, ensuring uniqueness for the email and compliance with password security standards. Upon successful validation and account creation, the system issues a JWT access token and a refresh token for authenticated access. This endpoint supports the customer actor's self-registration flow, incorporating security and validation logic per platform business rules. If any field (such as email or phone) is not unique or does not pass validation logic, the system returns a detailed error response referencing exact schema field constraints. The operation references the 'shopping_customers' table for account data, and leverages audit and session management via related tables.
operations.description:
This API operation enables the registration of a new customer account by accepting required fields defined in the 'shopping_customers' Prisma schema, including email, password_hash, name, and phone. The operation enforces uniqueness validation on the email field as described in the schema and implemented in database constraints. Upon creation, the system issues JWT access and refresh tokens for session management, utilizing the related session and token infrastructure. Account registration is subject to business logic requirements, including password complexity, real name verification, and phone number validation, all of which must conform to schema formats and constraints.

Integration with the shopping_customer_sessions table occurs post-registration to track session information, as customers receive tokens for immediate authenticated use. All validation of input data—such as proper email format and phone structure—relies on the schema-defined field properties and system-enforced rules for the 'customer' actor. Security best practices, including password hashing and audit trail generation, are employed by this endpoint.

Registrations resulting in errors, such as attempted duplicate emails (violating the '@@unique([email])' constraint), are handled gracefully by returning informative error messages referencing the violating schema field. Related operations include subsequent login or token-refresh, both of which consume the tokens issued here. All registration attempts are audited for compliance with platform and regulatory requirements, ensuring accountability as reflected in the schema's audit relations.
operations.summary: Register a new customer (shopping_customers table) and create JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Customer registration data, strictly matching 'shopping_customers' schema fields required for account creation.

responseBody.description: Authorized customer session, including JWT tokens and session metadata per 'shopping_customers' and session schema.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: This operation authenticates a customer on the shopping-mall platform by validating provided credentials (email and password). On successful authentication—using the data in the 'shopping_customers' Prisma schema and password verification—the operation issues new JWT access and refresh tokens for the customer. Session metadata is also recorded in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' table. Incorrect credentials (invalid email/password, inactive/deleted account) result in an error response referencing relevant schema fields. This operation implements robust account access control and aligns with the customer actor's security model.
operations.description:
This API endpoint authenticates a customer using 'email' and 'password_hash' fields as defined in the 'shopping_customers' schema. If the credentials match an active account, new JWT tokens are generated for session management. The operation references the schema's is_active and deleted_at fields to ensure only eligible accounts can access the system. Audit log and session creation are triggered in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' related table, using metadata such as IP address stored at authentication time.

Security is handled according to platform guidelines—hashing passwords on comparison and strictly matching the schema column formats. If the email is not found, the password is incorrect, or the account is marked deleted (deleted_at not null) or inactive (is_active false), the endpoint returns detailed authentication errors linked to schema field constraints.

Post-login, the endpoint issues JWT access and refresh tokens containing the customer ID, role, and permissions, drawing from the session management infrastructure described in the schema. Security, audit, and compliance requirements are enforced throughout.
operations.summary: Authenticate customer and issue tokens using 'shopping_customers' schema.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials ('email' and 'password_hash') referencing the 'shopping_customers' schema.

responseBody.description: Authorized customer session with JWT tokens and metadata as per schema.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: This operation refreshes the JWT access and refresh tokens for a customer, using a valid (previously issued) refresh token. It validates the refresh token in the context of the current 'customer' session, as persisted in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' schema, updating session metadata and issuing new tokens. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, revoked, or associated with an inactive or deleted account, an appropriate error response is returned referencing schema session or account fields. Token rotation logic matches security best practices and platform configuration for session management.
operations.description:
This endpoint handles the secure renewal of customer JWT tokens by validating an existing refresh token. It leverages the 'shopping_customer_sessions' and 'shopping_customers' schema to verify token validity, session state, and account activity. Upon validation, new access and refresh JWTs are generated and returned, with the session metadata updated accordingly in the schema. The operation enforces token expiration, revocation, and account validity, referring to is_active and deleted_at fields in the 'shopping_customers' schema for eligibility.

If validation fails due to token expiration, revocation, or customer inactivity or deletion, a detailed error message referencing the relevant schema constraint is returned. Security and traceability are prioritized, as audit logs are created for all successful and failed token refreshes according to the relationships laid out in the schema.

This endpoint is a critical component of the customer authentication flow, working closely with the login and join operations, and must be used after those endpoints have completed. The operation references all necessary schema fields and relationships for a complete and compliant token rotation infrastructure.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for a customer session using session and 'shopping_customers' schema.

requestBody.description: Refresh token and session data, based on schema for session and 'shopping_customers' actor.

responseBody.description: Renewed authorized session with new JWT tokens per schema.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation initiates a password reset request for an existing customer account. It requires the user to supply their registered email address. The system verifies the email against the 'shopping_customers' schema, and if valid, issues a time-limited secure reset token, which is logged in the 'shopping_password_resets' table, referencing schema fields 'request_email', 'reset_code', and 'expires_at'. No information is revealed if the email is not found for privacy. The endpoint supports secure customer password reset flows as per business requirements, aligning with audit, compliance, and communication workflows in the schema.
operations.description:
This endpoint lets a customer initiate a password reset by providing their email address, which is checked for existence and validity in the 'shopping_customers' schema. If an active account is found, a secure, time-limited reset token is generated and persisted in the 'shopping_password_resets' schema using 'request_email', 'reset_code', and 'expires_at' fields. The response does not disclose whether the email exists to prevent enumeration.

The operation only references schema fields and never exposes any customer data if the supplied email is not matched, to protect user privacy. Rate limiting, email delivery of reset links, and auditing are enforced per business and platform security policies using the relationships provided in the schema. The operation is closely related to password-update completion endpoints and is the entrypoint for secure recovery workflows for the customer actor.
operations.summary: Initiate password reset for customer using 'shopping_customers' and 'shopping_password_resets' schema.

requestBody.description: Customer email for initiating password reset, referencing the schema.

responseBody.description: Password reset token delivery confirmation, referencing schema fields only.

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: This operation completes the password reset process for a customer using the secure reset token issued in the previous step. It validates the reset token against the 'shopping_password_resets' schema ('reset_code', 'expires_at', 'consumed_at'), ensures it is not expired or already used, and updates the password_hash field for the target customer account in the 'shopping_customers' schema. Upon success, the reset token is marked as consumed and audit logs are created. Errors include invalid/expired token or, if applicable, security violations, always referencing relevant schema fields.
operations.description:
This endpoint finalizes customer password reset by verifying the secure reset token against the 'shopping_password_resets' schema fields ('reset_code', 'expires_at', 'consumed_at') and, if valid, updating the related customer's password_hash in the 'shopping_customers' schema. After updating the password, the token row is marked as consumed, with full auditing enforced as described in the schema's relationships. All error responses reference the exact schema validation that failed.

Business logic enforces password strength and secure handling, with email notification and session invalidation handled separately using schema relationships. This operation is always linked to a prior call to the password reset token initiation, and closely aligns with login and token refresh endpoints for full customer account recovery. Only explicit, existing schema fields are handled at all steps to ensure type and business logic correctness.
operations.summary: Finalize customer password reset by validating the token and updating 'shopping_customers' schema.

requestBody.description: Password reset token and new password, matching schema for resets and customer updates.

responseBody.description: Password reset success confirmation, referencing impacted customer schema fields.

operations.name: resetPassword

prerequisites.description: A password reset request must be initiated before a customer can complete the password reset process. This ensures a valid, time-limited reset token has been generated and exists in the shopping_password_resets schema before finalizing the password change.

operations.specification: Create a new seller account and immediately issue initial JWT tokens. The operation is targeted at the 'shopping_sellers' table, which stores core authentication credentials for sellers, including 'email' (unique, login identifier), 'password_hash' (secure password storage), 'display_name' (business name), 'contact_phone', 'status' (for onboarding workflow), and business logic attributes relevant to onboarding and account setup. The process requires minimal but essential seller information, including unique business email and a password; it captures all necessary data for initial authentication and business context creation. Email uniqueness is validated at account creation. This endpoint is used to sign up new merchants for participation on the platform, automatically creating an authenticated session upon successful registration. This endpoint can only be used for onboarding new sellers; it cannot be used for admin or customer registration. Registration supports required seller-specific fields as dictated by platform compliance and business onboarding logic. Account status will be set to 'pending' by default until admin verification of legal/business credentials completes. Non-unique emails are rejected with an explicit business-level error. On success, a JWT access token and refresh token are returned, encapsulated inside an authorized DTO structure. The API response references IShoppingSeller.IAuthorized, which contains the authorized seller profile and token set.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new seller in the 'shopping_sellers' table, requiring a unique business email, password (hashed), display name, and contact phone. Additional business verification fields such as business registration and legal entity information are completed after account creation, in separate flows. 

The operation enforces that provided emails are unique and not already registered, in accordance with 'shopping_sellers.email' being a unique indexed column. A password is provided as a plain string during registration and securely hashed before storage in the 'password_hash' field. The initial 'status' for the created seller account is set to 'pending', which triggers downstream compliance and admin review workflows, as mandated in onboarding requirements.

Security is a primary concern: passwords are never stored in plaintext, and registration errors do not reveal whether a given email is already in use. Upon successful creation, the seller is authenticated automatically, with JWT access and refresh tokens issued and returned in the authorized DTO structure.

Seller registration is limited to this endpoint; admin or customer accounts must use their respective endpoints. This endpoint does not permit bypassing post-onboarding verification flows – sellers must be approved by an admin before listing products or receiving payments. Error handling follows strict business patterns, returning actionable error codes for duplicate emails, invalid formats, or password strength violations.

This operation is related to the seller authentication (login) endpoint, the token refresh endpoint, and downstream business onboarding API operations (e.g., business info submission, document upload, compliance checks).
operations.summary: Register a new seller account (shopping_sellers) and issue initial JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: New seller registration information, including email, plaintext password, display name, and contact phone.

responseBody.description: Authorized seller profile and authentication tokens (JWT access/refresh), structured for immediate use.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate an existing seller by validating credentials and issuing new JWT tokens for access and refresh. The operation is mapped to the 'shopping_sellers' table, which holds seller authentication credentials (email and password_hash). This endpoint performs secure password validation using the hashed password stored for sellers, rejecting invalid credentials and enforcing business login policies such as account suspension/lockout and max attempt rate limiting as per 'is_active', 'status', and platform rules. Upon successful authentication, a JWT access token and refresh token are issued as part of the authorized DTO response. The operation does not return explicit authentication failure details that could be abused for enumeration. It is for sellers only; customers or admins must use their corresponding endpoints. The schema ensures secure, auditable, and compliant login according to all platform requirements.
operations.description:
This operation logs in a seller by validating email and password against the 'shopping_sellers' table. The email must exist and be unique (enforced by schema), and passwords are verified against the stored 'password_hash' using secure password comparison logic. The operation also checks the seller's account status (such as 'active', 'pending', 'suspended') and 'is_active' flag to ensure only eligible accounts can log in. If credentials are valid, a new JWT access token and refresh token are generated and returned inside the authorized DTO response struct (IShoppingSeller.IAuthorized).

Account lockouts are enforced after multiple failed login attempts, according to business policy, with any lockout status signaled using structured business error codes. This endpoint does not reveal whether a non-existent email is used for login, to prevent user enumeration. Success returns the complete seller authorization profile, while errors return actionable, business-friendly codes.

This endpoint is related to the registration ('join') and token refresh endpoints, as well as session management APIs. It does not handle password resets (handled via separate flows referencing shopping_password_resets). Audit trails are generated for all login attempts.
operations.summary: Authenticate seller (shopping_sellers) and issue JWT tokens upon successful login.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials: email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized seller profile and newly issued JWT tokens (access/refresh) after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh JWT access and refresh tokens for a seller using a valid refresh token. This operation interacts with the seller authentication and session model (shopping_seller_sessions) to validate and rotate refresh tokens, ensuring session security and compliance. It verifies the provided refresh token's validity, expiration, and revocation status (session not revoked or expired based on 'expired_at' in shopping_seller_sessions). If valid, it issues new tokens using the seller's profile, and returns them in the authorized DTO struct. Invalid or expired refresh tokens are rejected with standardized error codes. It is applicable to sellers only and does not serve customer or admin refresh operations. This workflow complies with all requirements for session token management in distributed authentication systems with rotating token patterns.
operations.description:
This operation allows a seller to refresh their JWT access and refresh tokens using a valid, non-expired refresh token, leveraging session records in 'shopping_seller_sessions'. The API validates that the provided refresh token corresponds to a currently valid, non-expired session for the seller (checked with the 'expired_at' field in the session record). If the refresh token is valid and the session is not expired or revoked, the API issues new tokens (access and refresh) and updates relevant session timestamps (where necessary), returning the new tokens in an authorized response DTO. If the refresh token is expired or invalid, the endpoint returns structured authentication error codes and does not issue new tokens.

This operation is strictly for sellers and is not available to customers or admins, who must use their own dedicated endpoints. All token refresh requests are securely audited and rate limited to mitigate abuse. This endpoint directly relates to the seller session management and login flows, as well as overall account security policy.

For password reset and account unlocking, sellers must use other endpoints managed via the password reset model (shopping_password_resets). Error handling is uniform and does not expose excessive details.
operations.summary: Refresh seller JWT tokens (access/refresh) using a valid refresh token, for shopping_sellers.

requestBody.description: Valid refresh token issued during seller authentication process.

responseBody.description: Updated authorized seller profile and new set of JWT tokens (access/refresh).

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Request a seller password reset by generating a secure, time-limited reset code and initiating the password reset workflow. Targets the 'shopping_password_resets' table, which links to the seller via 'shopping_seller_id', tracks the request email, reset code/token, expiration, and audit timestamps. Upon request, if the given seller email exists, a new password reset record is generated, and a reset code is issued and delivered via email. To protect privacy and security, the endpoint does not indicate whether a given email is registered; it always responds with a uniform generic message. Reset codes are time-limited; used/expired codes are purged by a background process. On success, the response structure is generic, confirming that the workflow (if applicable) has begun. The endpoint references IShoppingSeller.IResetPasswordRequest for structured input and IShoppingSeller.IPasswordResetResult for the generic output message.
operations.description: This operation enables sellers to initiate a password reset process by providing their registered email address. The system generates a new, unique, and secure reset code (token), creates a password reset request record in the 'shopping_password_resets' table, associating it with the seller's account. The reset token is valid for a short period (typically one hour) and must be consumed by the follow-up reset-completion endpoint. No information about the presence or absence of the recipient email is revealed to avoid enumeration attacks. Upon request, the system always responds with a generic success/failure message, regardless of actual email registration. All email delivery of reset codes is managed by platform operations. Expired or used codes are cleaned up as part of periodic background tasks.
operations.summary: Initiate password reset for seller (shopping_password_resets): request reset code via registered email.

requestBody.description: Email address for seller password reset request.

responseBody.description: Result of password reset initiation (generic message does not disclose if target account exists).

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: Reset the seller's password by validating a reset code issued by the password reset request endpoint and updating their password securely. This endpoint references both the 'shopping_sellers' table (for password change) and the 'shopping_password_resets' table (to validate and consume the reset code). It verifies the code is valid, unexpired, and unused, and then updates the 'password_hash' for the seller corresponding to the reset request. The reset code and password reset record are marked as consumed. This operation completes the password reset flow (separate from login/authentication). On success, a generic structured message confirms password update. Input and output are formalized as IShoppingSeller.IResetPasswordComplete and IShoppingSeller.IPasswordResetResult. Invalid or expired codes result in failure messages.
operations.description: This endpoint allows sellers to complete password reset by submitting the reset code received in their email and a new password. The endpoint checks that the code (token) exists in 'shopping_password_resets', is unexpired and not consumed. If valid, it updates the seller's 'password_hash' to the newly provided, securely hashed password. Once completed, the reset request is marked as consumed, and password change audit logs are generated. No authentication is required to call this completion endpoint, but all input data must be valid and not expired. The response is always a generic result and does not reveal details about account existence. This endpoint ties directly to the password reset request endpoint, and together they fulfill the full seller password reset lifecycle.
operations.summary: Complete password reset for seller by validating reset code and updating password.

requestBody.description: Password reset completion: email, reset code, and new password for seller.

responseBody.description: Generic result message for password reset completion.

operations.name: completePasswordReset

prerequisites.description: Password reset request must be initiated for the seller before completing the password reset process; the reset code validated in completion comes from a prior password reset request.

operations.specification:
This operation registers a new admin account within the shopping mall backend platform. It is intended for platform setup or when an existing super admin creates a new admin. The admin registration process requires a unique email, a strong password (represented securely by a password_hash in the database), a real name, and an assignment of an initial role (such as 'super', 'support', etc.). The registration also involves business status assignment (defaulting to 'active' unless otherwise specified) as defined in the schema. Admin registration may also include optional account-level attributes, but only fields present in the shopping_admins table are considered.

This endpoint connects directly to the shopping_admins table, referencing fields such as email, password_hash, name, role, and status. Only those fields which are defined in the Prisma schema are to be used in this registration process. All business logic around additional settings or MFA requirements is handled by dedicated endpoints; only the basic account creation logic is implemented here.

Security is critical for admin registration: the endpoint must ensure unique admin emails, secure password hashes, and audit trails of account creation. Registered admins will require separate MFA enablement via other workflows. Account creation issues, such as duplicate email, must return explicit errors.

Prerequisite APIs: None required, but this endpoint should only be accessible by an authorized superadmin/admin actor.

The resulting admin account will be available for login through separate authentication endpoints. On successful registration, a full admin account DTO minus sensitive fields is returned.

Other admin management functions (suspension, override, deletion) are out of scope of this endpoint, which is strictly for new account creation.
operations.description:
This operation enables registration of a new administrator for the shopping mall platform. The shopping_admins table defines the required fields: email (unique identifier for admin login and notifications), password_hash (securely stored password for authentication), name (real name for audit and communications), role (privilege level string for RBAC), and status (account state such as active, suspended, pending).

The endpoint ensures that only unique emails are registered, leveraging the shopping_admins.email unique constraint. Passwords are never stored as plain text, aligning with the password_hash field and security best practices. Additional admin attributes (such as MFA configuration) are handled separately and not within this registration flow.

Upon account creation, the admin is automatically assigned a role and an active status, unless specified otherwise by an authorized superadmin. Role assignment and status settings must match the permissible values supported by the shopping_admins table. If any required field is invalid or missing, the endpoint returns detailed error feedback.

Security measures enforced by this endpoint include confirmation of email uniqueness, the use of secure password hashing (never directly exposed), and dedicated audit logging via related tables. Only actors with sufficient privileges can invoke this operation.

Related operations include: login for admin authentication (handled via a different endpoint), update admin information, suspend/reactivate admin, and enable MFA for an admin account, all of which have their own workflows and endpoints. This operation serves as the dedicated entry point for onboarding new admin accounts on the Shopping Mall platform.
operations.summary: Register a new admin account in shopping_admins table for platform administration.

requestBody.description: New admin registration data. Only email, password_hash, name, role, and status fields are accepted as per shopping_admins schema.

responseBody.description: Admin authentication and authorization token upon successful registration. Contains JWT tokens and admin account details as per IShoppingAdmin.IAuthorized DTO.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This operation authenticates an existing admin user of the shopping mall platform by verifying the provided credentials (email and password). The operation references fields in the shopping_admins table: specifically, email and password_hash for validation, with status and role being checked to confirm the account is allowed to log in. On success, JWT access and refresh tokens are issued following platform policy, with the response following the IShoppingAdmin.IAuthorized DTO shape.

This authentication process also checks the admin's status against permissible states (such as 'active'), and supports account lockout/ban enforcement via the status field. Further security features such as MFA are managed through other endpoints. The password_hash is never exposed in the response, and all login activity is subject to audit logging through related domain tables. Account login failures (such as invalid credentials or suspended status) must result in explicit, actionable errors as per business requirements.

The endpoint is public, but it is only intended for actual admin account logins. Other mechanisms, such as session validation and token refresh, are available through separate endpoints. This operation is foundational for secure access to all admin functions in the system.
operations.description:
This operation enables a registered admin to authenticate and establish a new session on the platform. It is mapped to the shopping_admins table, which contains the necessary fields for authentication: email (unique login identifier) and password_hash (for credential validation). Status and role fields are validated to ensure only active admins are granted access. The operation checks that the status of the admin account is not suspended or pending, before issuing JWT tokens.

On successful login, the endpoint issues both access and refresh tokens as part of the IShoppingAdmin.IAuthorized DTO, enabling administration functions according to RBAC. The password_hash or other sensitive fields are never included in the response. Failed authentication, due to invalid credentials or account status, leads to appropriate error messaging. All login attempts are audit-logged for compliance and security analysis.

Other related API operations include join (registration for new admin), refresh (token renewal), and enableMfa (enabling multifactor authentication for the admin account), each handled on their own endpoints. This endpoint is critical for secure backend platform management access.
operations.summary: Authenticate and log in an admin account via shopping_admins table.

requestBody.description: Admin login request payload, containing email and password.

responseBody.description: Admin authentication and authorization token set if login is successful. Response matches IShoppingAdmin.IAuthorized DTO.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation enables secure refresh of JWT tokens for an already authenticated admin on the shopping mall platform. Mapping to the shopping_admins table, it validates the provided refresh token for the admin, cross-checking the account's status and role to ensure the admin is still allowed access. The core function is to safely rotate and re-issue access/refresh tokens, following security rules on token expiration and revocation (for example, immediate revocation on admin suspension).

The request body must reference a refresh token as required for token renewal. MFA settings and session tracking are handled independently of this endpoint; the refresh process itself works only for accounts whose status remains valid in shopping_admins. This operation is audit-logged for traceability, and only valid tokens are processed. On successful operation, new tokens and allowable claims are returned using the IShoppingAdmin.IAuthorized DTO, which describes a recognized, authenticated admin session.
operations.description:
Allows an authenticated admin to renew JWT access and refresh tokens. This process checks token validity, admin account status, and ensures the admin has not been suspended or deleted. Utilizes shopping_admins fields for identity validation, while ensuring no sensitive information is leaked in responses. Any misuse or expired tokens are reported with specific error codes.

The operation is mapped directly to the shopping_admins table for account validation, but does not read or mutate any fields other than those required for permission verification and session audit. Session and MFA configuration reside outside of this refresh path. The endpoint is part of the robust authentication model for admin actors.

Related endpoints include join (admin registration), login (admin authentication), and enableMfa (enabling multifactor authentication – handled on a separate endpoint). This refresh endpoint provides for rotation of tokens and session extension, integral for continuous administrator access while maintaining security boundaries.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for authenticated admins with valid refresh token, via shopping_admins table.

requestBody.description: Admin token refresh request parameters (must include the current refresh token).

responseBody.description: Renewed admin authentication and authorization tokens, conforming to IShoppingAdmin.IAuthorized DTO.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filtered list of system configuration entries from the shopping_system_configurations table. Supports advanced searching and filtering by config_key, config_value, creation or modification timestamps, and description contents (with full-text search using trigram indexes). Useful for administrators or DevOps teams to consume and audit platform configuration state. Ensures only current, active (non-deleted) configurations are returned, and supports sorting and pagination for large sets.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated, filtered list of system configuration entries (shopping_system_configurations).
operations.description:
This API operation is designed to enable administrators and DevOps users to search, filter, and retrieve platform-wide system configuration entries from the shopping_system_configurations table. Users can filter results by configuration key, value, and text-search any part of the configuration description, leveraging GIN trigram indexes for efficient matching and relevance ranking.

Each configuration entry includes critical details for platform operation, such as SMTP servers, feature flags, service endpoints, or runtime parameters. The operation provides pagination and supports ordering results by creation or update timestamps, making it suitable for integration into service dashboards or operational audit tools.

Security considerations: Only administrative actors can use this API, as exposure of configuration values could reveal infrastructure or security secrets. The provider will enforce role-based filtering so only active (non-soft-deleted) records are returned.

Related operations include: retrieval of individual configuration details by key, creation or updating of configuration values, and auditing or rolling back changes when errors occur. Error responses provide full diagnostic context for troubleshooting purposes. The operation never exposes configuration secrets other than as required by admin actor permissions.

requestBody.description: Advanced search, filtering, and pagination parameters for system configuration entries

responseBody.description: Paginated list of configuration entry summaries matching the search criteria

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single system configuration entry, identified by its unique config_key, from the shopping_system_configurations table. Used in admin settings UIs and service-level configuration loaders. Enforces strict permissions to prevent disclosure of sensitive configuration values except to authorized administrators or platform DevOps. Returns all fields of the matched configuration, including audit fields, provided the entry is not soft deleted.
operations.summary: Retrieve a system configuration entry by config_key (shopping_system_configurations).
operations.description:
This API operation returns full details for a single configuration entry in the shopping_system_configurations table, identified by its unique config_key parameter (case-insensitive). It is essential for admin dashboards and platform boot processes, such as loading SMTP settings, API URLs, or critical feature flags.

The operation ensures strict RBAC enforcement, only returning configuration data to authorized admin users. If the target config_key does not exist or is soft deleted, a 404-not found result is returned. Security controls mask or redact configuration secrets as defined in platform policies to avoid accidental credentials leakage.

The response payload contains all core configuration metadata (key, value, description, timestamps, deletion state) including documentation field for operations or deployment traceability. Related operations include list/search of all configuration entries, creation, update, and value history auditing. Care is taken to log all access to this endpoint for compliance and incident response.

If the key is missing, invalid, or does not match an existing (active) configuration entry, the response will follow platform error contract and include a clear indication of not found with audit reference.

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description: Unique system configuration key (case-insensitive, e.g. 'core.smtp_server'). (global scope)

responseBody.description: Full system configuration entry for the given config_key, or not-found error if unavailable.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new system configuration entry on the shopping mall platform. It operates on the shopping_system_configurations table and requires specifying a unique configuration key and configuration value. Each configuration helps manage core system settings such as feature flags, environment URLs, SMTP servers, or other runtime parameters essential for system operation. Only administrative actors should be authorized to invoke this endpoint since altering system configurations could affect global behavior. The configuration key must be unique and case-insensitive, and configuration values are stored as strings (may be JSON-encoded for structured data).
operations.summary: Create a new system configuration entry (shopping_system_configurations)
operations.description:
Create a new system-level configuration entry for platform runtime settings and control. This endpoint allows administrators to register a new configuration key and value pair, which might be used for controlling feature toggles, defining service URLs, SMTP connection details, or other cross-cutting settings.

Access to this endpoint should be restricted to admin users. Upon submission, the provided config_key is validated for uniqueness (case-insensitive and must not conflict with existing keys), and config_value is saved as provided. Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of password reset requests in the system. This operation enables administrators or security auditors to review password reset histories, identify recent or expired requests, and investigate suspicious activity.

The operation provides search and filter options, such as searching by email address, filtering by actor type (customer, seller, admin), and restricting results to a time window or showing consumed vs. unconsumed reset codes. Sorting and pagination are supported for efficient browsing of large log datasets.

This endpoint operates on the shopping_password_resets table, which logs all fields necessary for compliance and audit tracking. It operates on the shopping_products table and supports advanced querying by product name, description, code, seller, status, category, tags, price range, variant attributes, and catalog sorting rules. The access pattern facilitates business-facing use cases, such as customers browsing the catalog, sellers reviewing their own products, and admins managing product listings. The API design aligns with the business requirements for customer- and seller-facing catalog search and filtering, ensuring scalable performance and security alignment with actor permissions. It is designed to support wild-card keyword searching on product name and description, as well as precise filtering on product code, status, seller, and category. Advanced options include faceted filtering over associated tags and variant attributes, as well as multi-level sorts such as price ascending/descending, newest, or rating. 

Security controls ensure that only active (published) products are returned to customers. Sellers are enabled to search and filter on their own products, while admins have access to global product listings. Business logic supports only products with at least one active SKU, in line with the business requirements. Sensitive filtering (e.g., unpublished or archived products) is restricted to admins and sellers. Rate limiting may be applied for excessive search requests, and results are paginated according to API specification.

It leverages the shopping_products table in the Prisma schema, which contains all necessary information about a product, such as the seller's identification, business code, name, description, primary image URI, status, business_status, and timestamps. Upon creation, a business workflow around validation, status, and assignment to the catalog becomes active. The operation requires all mandatory product fields and expects that at least one variant (SKU) will be created in subsequent steps as per business rules. This endpoint is accessible to authenticated sellers and platform admins, following the catalog management permissions described in the requirements.
operations.description:
This API endpoint is designed for sellers (and platform admins) to create a new product entry in the catalog. The process requires the submission of all required fields, including product code, name, description, main image URI, current status, and business status. The request will be validated against the business catalog requirements, ensuring all mandatory data is present and the business code is unique.

Upon successful creation, the product is registered under the requesting seller's account, attached to a specific catalog, and prepared for linking with SKUs and attributes. Business and workflow status control visibility, so a draft or under_review product will not be publicly visible until approved and published. Attempts to create a product with a duplicate code or missing vital details will result in a validation error, and comprehensive error messages will be provided based on the rule violated.

Security measures enforce that only authenticated sellers or admins may invoke this operation, and all actions are auditable for compliance. The created product will be available for management through subsequent endpoints handling images, variants/SKUs, category assignments, and publishing workflows.

The product to be updated is specified by its globally unique business product code (code), ensuring clear and unambiguous resource identification. Business rules dictate that product codes are immutable once orders exist for the product, and attempts to update code in those cases will result in validation errors. Fields like name, description, images, status, business_status, and other updatable data can be modified as long as the product is eligible for changes per the business logic.

Authorization is restricted to the seller who owns the product and platform admins. All successful updates are logged for compliance, and any failed modification attempts due to business constraints (such as changing product code after order placement) will generate structured errors indicating the reason for denial.

Error scenarios such as forbidden access, invalid product code, or field violation are handled with business-specific and detailed response messages. This operation complements other product management endpoints (SKU and attribute management, category reassignment) in the platform's product lifecycle.

Security and authorization controls limit this endpoint to administrative actors. An appropriate permission check is performed to ensure only authorized admins execute such catalog-structure changes. Because categories are fundamental to browsing, search, and catalog integrity, any delete operation will also update hierarchical relationships of sibling and child nodes, maintain deterministic sort order for remaining categories, and may trigger downstream catalog update events for cache invalidation or UI refresh.

Only users who have inventory management permission for the SKU (owners, platform admins) can access this resource. Read access by sellers is restricted to their own SKUs.

The request supports advanced query parameters for audit/search purposes, including filtering by actor type (customer, seller, admin, system), date range, adjustment range, and free-text search of context notes. Pagination and sorting controls are available to efficiently browse large adjustment log histories. Users should inspect this audit log for troubleshooting stock discrepancies or reviewing compliance with inventory policies. Related error scenarios (e.g., unknown sku_code, unauthorized access) are surfaced with clear error messages.

This is the sole API for appending inventory change events; all increases, decreases, or corrections to SKU inventory must be performed via this endpoint. The operation enforces strict validation against the underlying SKU's existence, actor permissions, and business rules (no negative inventory, reason codes, and audit). The endpoint supports atomic recording and audit-compliance: every change must include actor identity, reason code, before/after quantities, and context notes as needed. Only sellers for their own SKUs, or admins, can make adjustments. Use cases include manual restocking, correction of stock anomalies, order- or refund-driven restocks, and system-initiated adjustments (performed as admin or system).

Append a new inventory adjustment record for a given SKU, documenting an atomic change in inventory (increase/decrease/correction) for auditing and operational accuracy. This API supports all legitimate business needs for changing inventory: restock by sellers, system correction by admin, order/return/refund reconciliation, and anomaly adjustments.

A valid adjustment request must specify the SKU by code, the adjustment amount (positive or negative integer), a business reason code, actor type, and any contextual notes. The server will validate that the actor is authorized to adjust this SKU (seller for own inventory, admin, or system actor). Adjustments that would result in negative inventory are strictly rejected and return a clear error. All fields (quantities before and after, actor, timestamp) are immutably stored on acceptance for compliance. For transactional consistency, the system applies the adjustment atomically and, if required by business rules, triggers downstream alerts or low-stock notifications. Error scenarios include unknown sku_code, lack of permission, invalid adjustment amount, and business constraint violations. Only authorized actors may use this endpoint; all events are audited.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve all inventory alerts for a specific SKU
operations.description:
Retrieve a list of all inventory alerts for a specified SKU by code. This includes both active and resolved alerts, allowing sellers or admins to monitor supply issues such as low stock, out-of-stock, manual overrides, or detected anomalies. 

The operation supports filtering by alert type, status (resolved/unresolved), date ranges for triggered or resolved events, and search by context note. Querying alerts is crucial for timely restocking and risk management, ensuring that inventory managers are notified of potential issues tracked by the Prisma schema. Result is paginated, with total alert count, alert details, and optional resolution context per alert.

This endpoint references the shopping_inventory_alerts table, which is closely related to the shopping_skus entity through the SKU code and to the underlying inventory monitoring system. Role-based access control can limit visibility: sellers only see their own SKUs, whereas admins have global scope for platform health monitoring.

parameters.name: skuCode
parameters.description: Globally unique business code identifying the target SKU (global scope)

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for inventory alerts related to the SKU, such as alert type, resolved status, and trigger/resolution date ranges.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of inventory alerts and their detailed information for the specified SKU.

A SKU must be created before inventory alerts can exist for that SKU. The SKU is identified by the skuCode parameter in the alert endpoint.

Supports search and filtering by alert type, resolved state, and trigger/resolution dates. The SKU code is required to identify which SKU's alerts will be queried. Alerts help sellers and admins monitor inventory state and take proactive action.

operations.description:
Retrieve full details of a single inventory alert identified by alertId for the given SKU code. This operation allows sellers and admins to review the root cause, timeline, context, and status updates for critical inventory signals related to a product variant.

The operation draws on the shopping_inventory_alerts table from the Prisma schema, ensuring that the requested alert exists for the specified SKU. The full context note, trigger events, resolution actions, actor metadata, and all timestamps are included. This is valuable for post-incident review, audit, or compliance purposes, and supports root-cause analysis or escalation workflows.

Access control ensures sellers may retrieve alerts for their managed SKUs, while admins may retrieve alerts platform-wide for investigation of inventory actions or audit events as tracked in the system.
