It queries the shopping_admin_suspensions table, enabling administrators to find and review all imposed suspensions on admin, seller, or customer accounts. Filtering can be performed by suspension type (temporary, permanent, pending_appeal, etc.), status (active, expired, revoked), actor (admin who imposed), affected entity, or effective date range. The results are sorted as specified in the request. This endpoint does not expose or allow editing of business-sensitive fields except for displaying compliance/audit reasons and statuses.

Retrieve a filtered, paginated, and sortable list of admin suspensions imposed across the shopping mall platform. This operation targets the shopping_admin_suspensions table and enables administrators to review actions taken against admin, seller, or customer accounts for compliance, audit, or security analysis.

The API allows optional search parameters such as suspension_type, status (active, expired, revoked, pending_appeal), start_at/end_at range, and references to either the enacting admin or the affected actor. Results are paginated, with configurable page size and sort options by start date, end date, or actor. Only actors with admin privileges may access this operation; the endpoint is not public or available for self-service by affected users or sellers.

This endpoint supports operational and compliance requirements by providing accountability and traceability for every suspension imposed on the platform. It enables advanced filtering and auditing for disputed or escalated actions and integrates with the overall admin operations and audit logging features described in accompanying requirements documentation.

Errors are returned for invalid filters, insufficient admin permissions, or attempts to access records outside the admin's visibility scope.

Create a new admin suspension event for a specified actor (admin, seller, or customer) on the platform. This operation is used by administrators to impose a temporary or permanent suspension for reasons such as policy violations, compliance issues, or business enforcement requirements.

The operation enforces required validation on who may be suspended, the type and duration of suspension, and ensures all necessary context and reason codes are included for auditability. Business rules such as preventing the suspension of oneself or the last remaining super admin are enforced.

Upon successful creation, the new suspension instance is returned for immediate display and further processing. Comprehensive error handling is applied: attempts to suspend non-existent users, duplicate suspensions, or invalid data will generate clear business error responses. Update details of an existing admin suspension in the system. All changes are subjected to business validation logic to ensure data integrity.

The operation will perform a hard delete as the schema lacks explicit soft-delete fields, thus ensuring that the targeted admin suspension entry is physically removed and cannot be recovered. Only system administrators with proper authorization should have access. The operation requires the unique identifier of the admin suspension record to identify and erase the corresponding entry.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a specific admin suspension record (shopping_admin_suspensions table).
operations.description:
This endpoint allows an authorized system administrator to permanently delete an admin suspension record by its unique identifier. This is a hard delete operation because the shopping_admin_suspensions table does not specify a soft-delete field, which means the record is fully expunged from the database and cannot be restored once removed.

requestBody.description: Information required to create a business constraint (unique constraint_name, scope, value, unit, description, activation state)

responseBody.description: Detailed information for the newly created business constraint

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates (edits) an existing business constraint in the shopping platform's constraint management table. It operates on the shopping_business_constraints table and allows platform administrators to modify any aspect of the constraint, including value, scope, limits, units, descriptive text, and activation status. The constraint to update is identified by its unique constraint_name (global scope). All validation for types, units, value changes, and name uniqueness is enforced at the API and database level.
operations.summary: Update an existing business constraint (shopping_business_constraints) by constraint name
operations.description:
This API allows platform administrators to edit and update an already-defined business constraint. The targeted constraint is globally identified by its unique constraint_name path parameter.

Typical updates include changing the limit_value, adjusting the applicable domain scope, modifying the constraint description for business clarity, transitioning activation state, or correcting the unit of measurement. The API operates with full validation on constraint types and value ranges. It will return validation errors if attempting to update a non-existent constraint, if the updated name or scope would collide with another, or if value/unit types do not match policy expectations.

Security and integrity are enforced by restricting access to platform admins, and all update actions are fully audited in administrative logs. The API's update operation maintains backward compatibility for dependent platform modules and ensures consistent enforcement of the latest business limits without introducing data inconsistencies.

parameters.name: constraintName
parameters.description: Unique business constraint name to identify the constraint entry (global scope)

requestBody.description: Updated information for the business constraint (scope, value, unit, description, activation state)

responseBody.description: Detailed information for the updated business constraint

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a business constraint configuration based on its unique constraint name. The associated table is shopping_business_constraints from the Prisma schema, which stores quantitative or policy limits applied to platform functionality (such as maximum order count per user, SKU count, etc.) per constraint name. Deletion is only permitted for existing, non-essential constraints and is a hard delete since the 'deleted_at' field is present (implement as soft-delete). This API ensures audit compliance and prevents accidental removal of essential platform guarantees by requiring an explicit constraint name identifier. All business rules regarding deletability must be enforced at the application level, checking for constraint dependencies before deletion is executed.
operations.description:
This API endpoint allows an administrator to mark a specific business constraint as deleted (soft delete) using its unique constraintName. The operation references the shopping_business_constraints model, where each constraint is uniquely identified by its constraint_name in the database.

Upon invocation, the system first validates that the provided constraintName exists and is eligible for deletion (for example, not a platform-required constraint). If the constraint is deletable, the operation sets the deleted_at timestamp, marking the constraint as inactive without physically removing it from the database. This approach maintains full retention for compliance and rollback. If the constraint does not exist or cannot be deleted due to business dependency or policy, a detailed business error should be returned, and no action is performed.

Sensitive operation: Only accessible to admin actors. All soft deletions are fully auditable and reversible by platform policy, and the endpoint is secured with strict authentication and action logging.
operations.summary: Soft delete (archive) a business constraint by unique constraint name in shopping_business_constraints table.

parameters.name: constraintName
parameters.description: Unique business constraint name of the target constraint (global scope). This must match the constraint_name column in shopping_business_constraints.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a list of all feature flags in the system with capabilities for advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting. It works on the shopping_feature_flags Prisma table, which stores feature switches for platform capabilities and A/B tests. The endpoint allows platform admins to search, filter by flag name, scope, and enabled status, and obtain overall feature toggle administration data.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows administrative users to search and retrieve the complete list of feature flags configured in the shopping mall platform. The shopping_feature_flags model supports global and context-specific feature toggles (enabling beta features, experiments, and rollouts by scope), and this operation enables comprehensive querying based on flag names, scopes, enabled states, and rollout percentages.

Administrators can use flexible filters within the request body, specifying criteria such as flagName, scope, enabled status, and pagination preferences (page number, limit, and sorting options). Paginated results ensure efficient retrieval regardless of catalog size, and each feature flag returned includes all flag metadata needed for platform control and auditing.

Security: Only admin actors can access this endpoint, and all actions are logged for compliance. The operation does not modify feature flags but provides read-only insight to manage the platform's feature control mechanisms.
operations.summary: Search, filter, and paginate feature flags for platform-wide feature management.

requestBody.description: Filter and pagination parameters for feature flag search (e.g., flag name, scope, enabled status, pagination and sort options).

responseBody.description: Paginated feature flag records matching filters, including all metadata from the shopping_feature_flags table.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of a specific feature flag by its unique flag code. It queries the shopping_feature_flags table in the Prisma schema, ensuring the flagName corresponds to the flag_code field, which uniquely identifies feature toggles managed by the admin users. This allows the frontend, admin panel, or deployment automations to assess whether a specific feature is enabled and if there is a planned rollout for experimentation or gated deployment. Only flags explicitly created and not soft-deleted are returned.
operations.summary: Retrieve a feature flag by flag code (shopping_feature_flags table)
operations.description:
Fetches detailed information about a feature flag, including its status (enabled or disabled), rollout percentage, description, and scope, by looking up the provided flagName (business code) against the shopping_feature_flags table. This operation enables platform code to dynamically check for feature enablement during runtime, supports gradual feature rollouts via percentage-based activation, and is essential for A/B experimentation, admin toggling, or business rule enforcement. 

This endpoint includes authentication and requires proper actor authorization to prevent unauthorized viewing or enumeration of feature toggles. Only admin users may retrieve feature flag definitions. 

Business validation includes confirming the flag is not soft-deleted and the flagName exists. Errors returned if the flag does not exist or access is denied. This operation integrates tightly with continuous delivery and admin dashboard interfaces. Relying on shopping_feature_flags's constraints, attempts to access a missing or deleted flag return an appropriate error, while valid lookups supply all fields needed for runtime toggling, experimentation, and audit logging.

parameters.name: flagName
parameters.description: Unique business code identifier for the feature flag (corresponds to flag_code in the shopping_feature_flags table; global scope)

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the feature flag corresponding to the flagName, including enablement, rollout, and description.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new feature flag in the shopping_feature_flags table. It allows platform administrators to add a new toggle for controlling feature rollout, experimentation, or business logic at runtime. During creation, fields such as flag_code, scope, enablement state, rollout percentage, and a description are required for proper flag operation and documentation. The endpoint ensures flag code uniqueness and appropriate value validation according to Prisma schema constraints. Used by admin panel interfaces or continuous delivery systems to add new feature flag controls.
operations.summary: Create a new feature flag (shopping_feature_flags table)
operations.description:
Allows administrative users to create a new feature flag entry by supplying all required fields as defined in the shopping_feature_flags table, including the flag_code (business identifier, unique), scope (context/domain for the flag), enabled state, optional percent-based rollout, and a business description. This operation is essential for managing rollouts of new features, enabling A/B testing, and improving operational safety during code deployments through runtime toggling. 

Strict validation ensures that the provided flag_code is globally unique and rejects creation if a flag with the same code already exists. Inputs are further validated to confirm the scope is provided and description is meaningful for admins and developers referencing the flag. This endpoint is for admin use only and enforces permissions at the controller level. Audit logging should be performed for all creation events. Upon success, the created feature flag entry is returned with all specified and system-generated fields populated. In case of validation or authorization errors, informative error messages are returned.

requestBody.description: Information needed to create a new feature flag, including unique code, scope, enablement, rollout percent, and admin-provided description.

responseBody.description: Created feature flag record, fully populated according to business policy and validation.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing feature flag in the platform's configuration subsystem. The feature flag entity, represented by the shopping_feature_flags table, allows administrators to enable, disable, or configure the rollout of platform features or experiments (such as beta features, domain-scoped rollouts, or temporary business toggles). The primary use case is to permit authorized actors (admins) to change the enabled state, rollout percentage, or other operational attributes for a specified flag identified by its unique flagName (used as flag_name in the schema). The operation should ensure that all business and compliance rules for feature flag modification are enforced, including audit logging of the actor and changes made. The operation explicitly targets the unique feature flag identified by the flagName path parameter, and is expected to validate input for business rule compliance and provide clear feedback on success or any constraint failures. Soft delete or archival behavior is not performed by this endpoint; it is strictly for update/overwrite actions.
operations.description:
Update an existing feature flag's configuration by specifying the flag's unique flagName and providing updated values for its attributes such as enabled state, scope, rollout percentage, and business description. This endpoint enables authorized admin actors to manage feature availability, A/B testing rollout, and domain-controlled enablement for the shopping platform. Business and compliance rules require that only admins can perform updates, and all changes must be fully auditable with actor/entity context recorded in the system logs.

The feature flag is identified by the flagName (string), which maps to the flag_name field in the shopping_feature_flags table. This endpoint allows modification of the enabled (Boolean), rollout (Float, optional), description (String), and scope (String) fields according to business policy. The endpoint enforces that flagName is unique and exists before any update occurs; attempts to update a non-existent or archived flag SHALL result in a clear error.

Proper validation must be performed to ensure logical and business constraints are not violated (e.g., rollout must be between 0 and 100, flagName must match an existing feature flag). This operation is critical for controlling live feature toggles and test releases across platform domains, supporting safe, controlled deployments and fast rollback in the event of issue discovery. Admin-only access is strictly enforced through authentication and role-based authorization mechanisms.
operations.summary: Update a feature flag's configuration in the shopping_feature_flags table by flagName (admin only).

parameters.name: flagName
parameters.description: Unique business identifier of the feature flag to be updated (global scope); this corresponds to the flag_name field and must be a string identifying an existing feature flag.

requestBody.description: Fields for updating feature flag configuration: enabled (Boolean), optional rollout (Float, 0.0–100.0), scope (String), and description (String). All fields are schema-validated for business rules and compliance.

responseBody.description: Full updated feature flag entity after modification, reflecting all new settings. Contains all fields and their updated values as defined in the IShoppingFeatureFlag DTO.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes (removes) a feature flag from the system, identified by its unique flagName (flag_name). The operation acts on the shopping_feature_flags table. Deletion is hard delete and not a soft-delete or archival; once deleted, the feature flag cannot be used for feature toggling or rollout logic. Audit logging of the operation and requester is enforced by business compliance policy. The endpoint requires admin-level authorization and should validate the flag's existence prior to deletion, providing a not-found error if necessary. This operation is for system administration and compliance cleanup, not for day-to-day operational use.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a specified feature flag from the system, using its global flagName as the identifier (corresponding to the flag_name field in the shopping_feature_flags table). This endpoint is restricted to admin actors and enforces audit logging of all delete actions for compliance and traceability. Attempting to delete a non-existent, already deleted, or in-use flag will produce clear errors as defined by business policy.

This delete operation is irreversible and removes all configuration, rollout, and enablement data for the feature flag. It is suitable for cleanup of deprecated, obsolete, or invalid feature toggles, and not for soft-deletion or archival: once removed via this endpoint, the flag cannot be restored and must be recreated if needed. Security checks ensure only admins can invoke this action and that all deletion events are logged in the platform's administrative audit logs for regulatory and support review.

This operation is critical for compliance and operational hygiene, ensuring that obsolete or deprecated feature toggles do not persist and inadvertently affect business logic or application flow. Admin permissions must be strictly enforced; business rules also require clear user feedback if the flagName does not exist or cannot be deleted due to in-use constraints.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a feature flag (flag_name) from the shopping_feature_flags table by flagName (admin only).

parameters.name: flagName
parameters.description: Unique business identifier of the feature flag to be deleted (global scope), corresponding to the flag_name field in the database.

operations.name: erase

IShoppingCustomer.ICreate.description: Request body schema for registering a new customer account in the shopping mall platform. This DTO enables customer self-registration by enforcing all business and security rules described in the business requirements and aligned with the Prisma 'shopping_customers' model. Includes all required fields for creating a new customer (email, password, name, phone), omitting system-managed properties (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and authentication context fields, per API security standards. On submission, backend handles password hashing and enforces unique constraint on email. This schema aligns strictly to the definition of 'shopping_customers' in the database: email string (unique, required), password string (plain text, strong, required), name string (required), and phone string (required). Additional session context fields (href, referrer) must be included to record login context for session and audit purposes, as per platform authentication flows.

email.description: Unique email address for the customer. Must be properly formatted and unique within the system, matching the Prisma @@unique([email]) constraint. Used for authentication and notifications.

password.description: Customer's plain text password (will be hashed on backend). Must meet platform password complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters, up to 128, with recommended use of uppercase/lowercase/digits/special characters.

name.description: Full name of the customer, used for personalization and delivery. Required by business rules.

phone.description: Primary phone number for the customer (digits, may include '+', dashes, spaces). Must be unique across all accounts and pass validation rules for structure and length.

href.description: Connection URL at registration time, required for session context and audit logging. Captured from client and stored in session record. Required by authentication operation.

referrer.description: Referring URL/page at registration time, required for session context and audit logging. Cannot be omitted. Captured from client.

oneOf.description: Client IP address at time of registration for audit/session context. Optional – server extracts if not provided.
Client IPv6 address (alternative to IPv4 format). Optional.

ip.description: Client IP address for session context and audit. Optional (server can infer); if present, must be a valid IPv4/IPv6 string or null.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated customer (shopping_customers.id).

email.description: Customer email.

name.description: Full name of the authenticated customer.

phone.description: Primary customer contact phone, formatted to local standard. Used for order notifications and delivery contacts. From shopping_customers.phone.

is_active.description: Indicates if the authenticated account is currently active. Reflects shopping_customers.is_active.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion timestamp for the account. If null, account is active in business logic. Used for GDPR/business retention, as per shopping_customers.deleted_at.

created_at.description: Timestamp at which the customer account was created. Used for auditing and analytics.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for last account data update. Reflects profile/contact/modification events.

role.description: Constant role value for this actor (always 'customer').

IShoppingCustomer.IAuthorized.description: Response DTO for customer authentication (login/refresh). Contains customer identity, session JWT tokens, and select customer fields for authenticated context.

email.description: Customer email address for authentication. Must be a valid, unique email as stored in the shopping_customers schema.

password.description: Plain text password for authentication. The backend validates this against the hashed value stored in the shopping_customers table. Minimum 8 characters, must meet platform's password strength requirements.

ip.description: Client IP address from which the session is initiated. This value is recorded in shopping_customer_sessions.ip and used for audit and security monitoring. Optional: Server can extract automatically.

href.description: URL where the login request was initiated (current page). Required for session context and audit; recorded in shopping_customer_sessions.href.

referrer.description: Referring page or source that initiated the login. Required for session context. Captured in shopping_customer_sessions.referrer.

IShoppingCustomer.ILogin.description: Customer login credential schema. Used to authenticate a customer actor based on email and password (plain text). Schema fields map directly to shopping_customers; session context (ip/href/referrer) are recorded in shopping_customer_sessions. Follows security and audit requirements for cross-platform traceability. DO NOT add password_hash—this is application-side logic only, not a request property.

refresh_token.description: The current, valid JWT refresh token previously issued to the customer. Used to identify the session being refreshed. Must exactly match the stored value for the session in shopping_customer_sessions.

ip.description: Client IP address from which the token refresh is requested. This value is recorded in shopping_customer_sessions.ip and used for audit and security monitoring. Optional.

href.description: URL where the refresh request was made (current page). Required for session context and audit; recorded in shopping_customer_sessions.href.

referrer.description: Referring page or source that initiated the token refresh. Required for session context. Captured in shopping_customer_sessions.referrer.

IShoppingCustomer.IRefresh.description: Schema for refreshing customer JWT tokens. Accepts a refresh_token (existing valid session token), and the session context for audit/compliance as tracked in shopping_customer_sessions. Ensures compliance with token rotation and security audit policies.

request_email.description:
Email address of the customer requesting password reset. Must match an existing, active customer account in the 'shopping_customers' table. Used for password reset initiation and auditing workflows.

Referenced directly in the password reset business process and is never exposed in responses. This field is case-insensitive and must be validated for format and existence.

IShoppingCustomer.IRequestPasswordReset.description: Request body for initiating a customer password reset. Represents only the email input field required to identify the customer in the 'shopping_customers' schema, and to log the request in 'shopping_password_resets'. The system accepts this DTO for entrypoint into the password reset workflow. No additional business data accepted.

confirmation.description: Always true if the password reset process was initiated for a valid email address. This value does not disclose email validity to callers, for privacy and security. Always returns true for any properly formatted request.

IShoppingCustomer.IPasswordResetInitiate.description: Confirmation response when a password reset request has been initiated by a customer. Does not disclose the existence of the email address in the system, and always returns { confirmation: true } for privacy, audit, and business policy reasons. No sensitive data is included in the response.

IShoppingCustomer.ICompletePasswordReset.description:
This schema defines the request body for the final step of a customer password reset workflow in the shopping mall platform. It is used to submit a secure, time-limited reset token (issued previously during the password reset initiation step) and a new desired password for the customer account. The backend validates the reset token by referencing the `shopping_password_resets` schema and, on success, updates the customer's password in the `shopping_customers` table. Business logic enforces password strength requirements and ensures secure credential handling throughout this process.

Upon successful completion, the reset token is marked as consumed and relevant audit logs are created for traceability. All field values must match format, uniqueness, and security constraints as per platform policy.

Properties:
- reset_code: Unique, time-limited code for password reset, cross-referenced to the reset request in the system (see `shopping_password_resets.reset_code`).
- new_password: The new plain-text password for the customer account. Must meet current platform strength and security requirements. This will replace the existing password (hashed) in `shopping_customers.password_hash` upon successful reset.

See operation and business requirements for additional audit, error, and session invalidation logic triggered by this call.

reset_code.description: The unique, time-limited password reset token issued to the customer as part of the password reset workflow. This must match an active (unexpired, unused) record in the `shopping_password_resets` schema (`reset_code`). Used to securely identify the password reset request to be finalized.

new_password.description: The new plain-text password to be set for the customer account. The backend will validate this password for minimum length, strength, and policy compliance, then securely hash and save it to the `shopping_customers.password_hash` field. Used for full credential replacement at account recovery.

IShoppingCustomer.IPasswordResetComplete.description:
Represents the successful outcome of a customer password reset operation within the account recovery workflow. Returned as the standard response body after the system verifies and applies a valid reset code (from the request), sets the new password, and marks the relevant password reset record as consumed in the audit trail. Implements strict auditing for both customer security and compliance purposes.

Properties:
- success: Boolean indicating whether the password reset and credential change was accepted and applied without error.
- customer_id: The unique identifier of the customer whose password was reset (referencing the affected row in `shopping_customers` by UUID).
- reset_token_consumed_at: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this password reset request was marked as consumed in the system's persistent audit log (`shopping_password_resets.consumed_at`). Used for audit and security tracking.

This response is designed for both user experience (confirmation) and back-office auditing and compliance, strictly aligning to schema and business policy.

success.description: Indicates whether the password reset operation was successfully completed and the customer's password updated as intended. Returns true only if all validation, audit, and transactional steps succeeded.

customer_id.description: UUID identifier of the customer whose password was changed. Sourced directly from the `shopping_customers` schema. Migrates completion context and enables back-end audit traceability for credential changes.

reset_token_consumed_at.description: Timestamp in ISO 8601 format recording the precise instant when the password reset request was finalized and the reset token marked as consumed. Sourced from the `consumed_at` field of `shopping_password_resets`. Used for security auditing and workflow validation.

email.description: Business email for seller login and verification. Must be unique and is used as the principal identifier for the seller account. Required as per 'shopping_sellers.email' schema column.

password.description: Plaintext password for seller registration. This will be securely hashed before being stored in 'password_hash'. MUST satisfy password strength requirements as per platform policy. Never returned in responses.

display_name.description: Public-facing business or shop name. Displayed to buyers and used in catalog and order communications. As per 'shopping_sellers.display_name' schema column.

contact_phone.description: Primary business contact phone for the seller, used for onboarding, transactional notifications, KYC, and customer support. Must comply with country-specific phone number formats.

status.description: Seller account business status. Always set to 'pending' on registration; not user-modifiable at onboarding. On creation, the seller account enters review, and status change is only permitted by admin actors per compliance requirements.

IShoppingSeller.IJoin.description: DTO for registering a new seller account in the shopping mall platform. Contains fields required for account creation and authentication. The 'status' field is always set to 'pending' on account creation and cannot be provided by the user. After registration, business verification (KYC, compliance) is performed before seller is activated. All onboarding and account eligibility rules are enforced as per the Prisma 'shopping_sellers' model and platform onboarding procedure.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated seller (shopping_sellers.id primary key; UUID).

email.description: Seller's registered email address (principal login identifier).

display_name.description: Business/shop public display name associated with the seller.

contact_phone.description: Primary phone number for business contact and notification.

status.description: Current status of the seller account (e.g. 'pending', 'active', 'suspended'). Set to 'pending' immediately upon registration as per onboarding and compliance workflows.

is_active.description: Indicates if the authenticated seller account is currently active and allowed to log in. Reflects shopping_sellers.is_active. Only active sellers are permitted to access seller features; suspended or inactive sellers are denied platform access or business operations.

created_at.description: Seller account creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC).

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp for the seller profile.

IShoppingSeller.IAuthorized.description: This DTO is returned by seller registration, login, and token refresh endpoints. It includes key seller profile information and the issued JWT access and refresh tokens, allowing for immediate authenticated access to the platform. The 'status' field reflects platform onboarding or compliance workflow stage (pending, active, suspended), and 'is_active' indicates if the seller account is permitted to access business features.

IShoppingSeller.ILogin.description:
DTO for seller login (authentication) request. Supplies email and password credentials for secure authentication against the shopping_sellers table. The password is supplied as a plain string (never pre-hashed), which will be checked against the stored password_hash in the database using secure comparison logic. Does not permit passing of session, identity, or status fields; only business credentials. This type is used only for seller authentication flows, NOT for registration or general seller CRUD.

Field requirements and validation, including email uniqueness/format and password security, are enforced at the API/service layer, not the schema itself. On successful login, the backend will issue JWT access/refresh tokens for the seller. The system enforces secure audit trails, login lockouts, and other business authentication controls as documented in requirements. (See shopping_sellers in Prisma schema for account details and unique constraints.)

email.description: Seller's login email. Must correspond to an active account in shopping_sellers, unique per platform. Used as the sole login identifier. Must follow standard email format and be case-insensitive. Required for authentication.

password.description: Seller account password (plain text, NOT pre-hashed). Must be at least 8 characters (backend enforces complexity/password quality per requirements). Will be securely compared to the password_hash stored for the given email in shopping_sellers.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for authentication tracking, audit, and potential fraud analysis. May be supplied by the client or derived by the API gateway; always stored or logged for session. Optional: If not provided, backend must attempt to derive from request context.

ip.description: Client IP address for authentication tracking, audit, and fraud analysis. May be supplied by client (SSR) or by API gateway, else left null and inferred backend-side. Optional for SSR/API-based logins.

href.description: The fully-qualified URL where the login request originated (page where login form submitted); captured for security audit and session creation context (shopping_seller_sessions.ip/href/referrer). Required, must be provided by client.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page/user journey event) at authentication time. Used for security audit trail and abuse/fraud tracing (shopping_seller_sessions.referrer). Required, must be supplied by client.

IShoppingSeller.IRefresh.description: DTO for refreshing JWT tokens for a seller actor using an existing (still valid & non-expired) refresh token/session. This object is submitted by sellers to issue new access/refresh tokens during active authenticated sessions. The only field required is the current valid refresh token. No account information, passwords, or session context fields are allowed or needed. Security and session integrity are managed by backend using the supplied token, not by exposing seller credentials in this DTO.

refresh_token.description: Existing valid refresh token previously issued during seller login or prior token refresh. Must be a signed, platform-scoped value matching a still-active session in shopping_seller_sessions and not expired or revoked. Format varies per JWT/session signing strategy (may be a JWT, Opaque, or similar). Required.

email.description: The seller's email address registered with the platform. Used to identify the seller account and initiate the password reset process. Must be a valid, properly formatted email address. This is cross-referenced to 'shopping_sellers.email' and is unique per seller.

IShoppingSeller.IResetPasswordRequest.description:
Request body DTO for initiating a seller password reset. Used by the password reset request endpoint to allow a seller to request a reset token sent to their business email address. This process does not disclose whether an email is registered to avoid enumeration attacks.

This DTO is used as the input for the POST /auth/seller/password/request-reset endpoint. It contains only the email property, as no additional information is required or disclosed at this stage.

message.description: A generic status message indicating that the password reset workflow has been initiated, without disclosing account existence for privacy reasons. Always included to provide a consistent API response regardless of input validity.

IShoppingSeller.IPasswordResetResult.description: Generic response DTO returned after initiating or completing the seller password reset flow. Does not indicate whether the email exists, or if the reset code is valid, for security and privacy best practices. Used as the standardized output for both the password reset request and completion endpoints.

email.description: Seller email for login and password reset. Must match an active account in the system. Must be a properly formatted email and match the unique constraint on shopping_sellers.email.

reset_code.description: Password reset code/token received via the password reset request flow. Must match a code in shopping_password_resets, be unexpired and unconsumed. Reset code is a secure, high-entropy, limited-use string. The system enforces length and uniqueness.

password.description: The new password (plain text in request DTO; will be securely hashed for storage). Must be 8–128 characters, contain uppercase/lowercase letters, numbers, and a special character to comply with platform password complexity policy. The backend securely hashes passwords before updating shopping_sellers.password_hash. Never accept weak or unvalidated passwords via API; all business constraints (length, character classes, forbidden contents) must be enforced at backend or validation middleware.

IShoppingSeller.IResetPasswordComplete.description: DTO for completing seller password reset. Used by sellers to submit email, reset code, and new password, as part of the password reset completion endpoint. The DTO enables validation of the code, checks for expiry and uniqueness (unconsumed), and registration of the new password, which must comply with platform complexity policy (8–128 chars, mixed character classes as documented in requirements/business rules). Email and reset code must match a valid, unexpired, and unused token in shopping_password_resets. Completed requests are marked as consumed, and passwords are never stored plaintext. All changes are audit-logged.

email.description: Unique admin email address for login and platform notifications. Minimum 5, maximum 100 characters. Must be a valid, properly formatted business email per RFC 5322, and must not be registered already (unique in shopping_admins.email). Used as the sole login identifier for the admin account and for all notifications, audit logs, and platform identity. Enforced by DB unique constraint and middleware validation.

password.description: Admin account password in plain text for initial registration; will be securely hashed before storing in password_hash. Must be 8–128 characters in length and meet platform password complexity requirements: include uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special characters. Only accepted if validated per security policy; never stored plain. Failure to comply with security constraints must cause validation failure.

name.description: Real name of the admin for audit trail and communications. Required for audit and business context. Field is stored for all log/audit interactions with a maximum of 100 characters.

role.description: Privilege level (e.g., 'super', 'support', 'compliance', 'operator'), as defined by platform RBAC policy and business documentation. Role assignment is validated against the shopping_admins privilege model at account creation/update. Only permitted values are accepted. Used in all access control checks and audit trails.

status.description: Initial business status of the admin account (e.g., 'active', 'suspended', 'pending', 'locked'). Acceptable values and default status ('active') are defined per platform business and audit/prima database rules. This field determines login and operation permissions for the admin. All status transitions are audit-logged; invalid/unauthorized status values will cause registration failure.

IShoppingAdmin.IJoin.description: DTO for registering a new admin account in the shopping mall backend. Used to create an account with a unique, business-email identifier (enforced via DB unique constraint), a secure, complex password (8–128 chars, must meet platform password policy), a real name for audit trail (max 100 chars), a privilege role as per valid RBAC/permission policy (min 2, max 32 chars, must be known/allowed), and an initial status ('active', 'pending', 'suspended', etc.) with allowed values per requirements. Only fields in shopping_admins schema may be provided. All values are strictly validated; purpose is onboarding highly privileged accounts in a secure, audit-compliant manner. Account creation, field values, and all events are recorded in the audit trails and logs. MFA is configured separately.

email.description: Admin login email. Unique identifier for authentication according to shopping_admins.email. Must be a valid business email address.

password.description: Admin password. Plain text value to be verified against shopping_admins.password_hash (backend will hash). Minimum security requirements (length, complexity) are enforced by business logic.

ip.description: Optional IP address for session context and audit logging. If not supplied, the server will capture IP automatically from request.

href.description: URL where the login is performed (session context, mandatory for audit).

referrer.description: Referrer page URI at session creation (mandatory for session audit compliance).

IShoppingAdmin.ILogin.description: Request DTO structure for authenticating and establishing a login session for an administrator on the shopping mall platform. This schema mandates supply of a unique admin email and password, along with session context fields (href, referrer), and optionally the client IP. The structure is mapped to the shopping_admins table for credential and status checks (no password hashes are exposed), and enforces business logic for secure credential validation and audit logging of all authentication activity. Use as the body for POST /auth/admin/login. All properties and contextual metadata are required for both security and compliance; success/failure logging is supported through session and audit tables as defined by the platform's business requirements and security policy.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin. Corresponds to shopping_admins.id. Used for traceability and session management.

email.description: Login email of the admin. Used for identification in application and session management. Matches shopping_admins.email.

name.description: Admin's real name. Used in communications, audit logs, and dashboard presentation. Sourced from shopping_admins.name.

role.description: Admin privilege level/role. Controls RBAC within application. Derived from shopping_admins.role.

status.description: Admin account status, e.g., 'active', 'suspended', etc. Enforces business policy. Sourced from shopping_admins.status.

created_at.description: Timestamp the admin account was created. Maps exactly to 'created_at' in shopping_admins.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update to the admin account (profile edit, role/status change, etc). Maps to 'updated_at'.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion marker for this admin. If not null, the account is logically deleted/disabled (per audit/compliance policy). Maps to 'deleted_at'.

IShoppingAdmin.IAuthorized.description: Detailed DTO returned when an administrator successfully registers, logs in, or refreshes authentication tokens within the shopping mall platform. This schema provides the complete authenticated admin account context, including identity, business status, privilege role, timestamps, and the JWT token envelope covering access/refresh flows. Designed for use as the return body in join/login/refresh endpoints, this structure is security audited and adheres to platform RBAC. Sensitive credential details (e.g., password hash) are strictly excluded. The token property includes both access and refresh tokens per platform authentication policy, supporting secure session management for critical admin platform activity.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token for the admin, required to renew JWT access and refresh tokens. Must be a valid, non-expired token issued to an administrator. Token validation is handled per shopping_admins session and security policy.

IShoppingAdmin.IRefresh.description: DTO for admin refresh token operation. This DTO must include the refresh_token field (snake_case for consistency with customer/seller refresh DTOs). It is used to renew access/refresh tokens for authenticated admins based on a submitted refresh token. Sensitive account validation and MFA are handled independently. No login credentials are accepted here.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based index), used to return a specific result page of the system configuration entries.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Limits the returned system configuration entries to this page size. Max value 100.

search.description: Optional full-text search keyword for filtering configuration keys, values, or descriptions using trigram search.

oneOf.description: Sort results by one of the supported columns: created_at (default), updated_at, or config_key.
Sort results by one of the supported columns: created_at (default), updated_at, or config_key.
Sort results by one of the supported columns: created_at (default), updated_at, or config_key.

sortBy.description: Sort results by one of the supported columns: created_at (default), updated_at, or config_key.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction: 'asc' for ascending (default), 'desc' for descending.
Sort order direction: 'asc' for ascending (default), 'desc' for descending.

sortOrder.description: Sort order direction: 'asc' for ascending (default), 'desc' for descending.

configKey.description: If set, filters results to configurations with an exact match on config_key.

configValue.description: If set, filters results to configurations with an exact match or partial match on config_value.

createdFrom.description: Optional lower bound for created_at filter (ISO 8601 datetime).

createdTo.description: Optional upper bound for created_at filter (ISO 8601 datetime).

description.description: If set, filters results to configurations containing this text in the description.

IShoppingSystemConfiguration.IRequest.description: Advanced search, filtering, and pagination parameters for system configuration entries (shopping_system_configurations). Supports full-text, field-based, and paginated queries for admin access to platform configurations.

IShoppingSystemConfiguration.title: System Configuration Entry
IShoppingSystemConfiguration.description:
Represents a single global system configuration key/value pair for platform-level settings, as defined in the shopping_system_configurations table. Used for deployment and runtime configuration (such as feature flags, SMTP, third-party API URLs). Each entry consists of a unique config_key (case-insensitive), associated value (config_value), and optional documentation (description). Includes audit metadata and soft-deletion status for traceability and compliance. Access to configuration entries is restricted to authorized administrative actors due to sensitivity of potential credentials or platform parameters.

Properties:
- id: The unique identifier (UUID) for this configuration entry. Maps directly to the 'id' PK in shopping_system_configurations.
- config_key: Unique, case-insensitive key for this setting (e.g., 'core.smtp_server'). Must be unique and unambiguous per platform instance.
- config_value: Arbitrary configuration value text (may be JSON-encoded for complex settings).
- description: Optional documentation of the purpose and business context of the setting.
- created_at / updated_at: Audit timestamps for lifecycle tracking.
- deleted_at: Timestamp for soft deletion (if not null, entry is archived/inactive).

id.description: Primary key UUID for this configuration record. Auto-generated by the database.

config_key.description: Unique system configuration key (case-insensitive, e.g., 'core.smtp_server'). Required, immutable once set.

config_value.description: The raw configuration value as text (may be JSON-serialized for structured config).

oneOf.description: Optional business/context documentation of what this config controls and how it is used. Nullable.

description.description: Optional business/context documentation of what this config controls and how it is used. Nullable.

created_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when this configuration was initially created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) for latest modification to this configuration entry.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion marker. When populated, entry is archived or logically deleted, but retained for historical purposes.

IShoppingSystemConfiguration.ICreate.title: Create System Configuration Entry Request
IShoppingSystemConfiguration.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new platform system configuration entry, as defined in the shopping_system_configurations table. Used by administrative actors to register global settings for feature toggles, third-party integrations, SMTP, and other runtime parameters.

Security & Validation:
- Only available to admin/DevOps actors.
- config_key must not duplicate existing or soft-deleted keys (case-insensitive).
- config_value may be any text (stringified JSON, plain string, etc), but business logic must enforce valid input for the given config type.
- Optional description should clarify the business purpose and operational significance of the key.

Properties:
- config_key (required): Globally-unique text key for system config.
- config_value (required): Value for the config setting.
- description (optional): Human-readable documentation annotation.

config_key.description: Required. Unique text key (case-insensitive) which identifies this system configuration entry, e.g., 'core.smtp_server'.

config_value.description: Required. String value to assign for this config key (may be plain text or JSON-encoded for complex values).

oneOf.description: Human-readable documentation explaining the business role, purpose, or usage constraints of this configuration setting.

description.description: Human-readable documentation explaining the business role, purpose, or usage constraints of this configuration setting.

config_value.description: Configuration value (serialized as text, may be JSON or string). Represents the updated value to apply for the configuration entry.

description.description: Optional revision to the business/context note explaining the configuration purpose or its operational intent. Used for business and admin audit, UI display.

IShoppingSystemConfiguration.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for system configuration entries in the shopping_system_configurations table. This type matches the requirements for admin-driven PUT operations that update the value and description of an existing configuration identified by its unique config_key (passed in the path).

- Only config_value and, optionally, description can be updated. The config_key is provided in the endpoint path and must reference an existing configuration.
- Aligns with audit and global system settings management use cases as defined in the business and technical requirements.

See shopping_system_configurations in the Prisma schema for base property documentation.

setting_key.description: Partial or case-insensitive match for the business setting key (e.g., currency, country). Optional filter, may be omitted for broad searches.

setting_value.description: Substring or pattern to match for business setting value (e.g., 'KRW', 'USD'). Optional filter for value field.

description.description: Substring or pattern to match against the description/comments in shopping_business_settings. Optional for full-text filtering.

created_before.description: Return only business settings created before this timestamp (ISO 8601 format). Optional.

created_after.description: Return only business settings created after this timestamp (ISO 8601 format). Optional.

updated_before.description: Return only business settings last updated before this timestamp (ISO 8601 format). Optional.

updated_after.description: Return only business settings last updated after this timestamp (ISO 8601 format). Optional.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Defaults to 1 if omitted.

page_size.description: Number of items per page (max 100). Defaults to 20 if omitted.

oneOf.description: Field by which to sort results. Enum: setting_key, created_at, updated_at.
Field by which to sort results. Enum: setting_key, created_at, updated_at.
Field by which to sort results. Enum: setting_key, created_at, updated_at.

sort_by.description: Field by which to sort results. Enum: setting_key, created_at, updated_at.

oneOf.description: Sort order: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Sort order: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort order: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

IShoppingBusinessSetting.IRequest.description:
Search/filter DTO for advanced querying of business settings in the shopping_business_settings table.

Supports flexible filtering, full-text search, partial matches by business key, value, and description, and time window constraints on creation/update. Pagination and sorting parameters provided for admin dashboard and operational use cases. Fields align directly with business settings Prisma schema.

All properties are optional and may be combined to create precise admin filters for audit or oversight.

IShoppingBusinessSetting.description:
Business setting entity representing a platform-wide operational configuration row, mapped to the 'shopping_business_settings' table in Prisma. Each setting controls a critical parameter for platform operation, such as default currency, region, taxation policy, or specific regulatory toggles. The entity is uniquely identified by its business 'setting_key' (string), and only one record per key is permitted, ensuring unambiguous system configuration management.

This DTO exposes all relevant fields for a business setting, including the business key ('setting_key'), value ('setting_value'), an optional rich description (for business context or documentation), and auditability via creation, update, and soft-delete timestamps. The canonical use case is for system initialization, operational dashboards, admin controls, and business logic enforcement, as described by the database schema. Settings are generally managed by administrators and are immutable with respect to their key -- updates replace value and description only. All timestamp fields correspond directly to those in the database table, so only those present in the Prisma schema are included. Deleted records (i.e., soft-deleted where 'deleted_at' is non-null) are excluded from the main API responses by business contract.

id.description: Primary key of the business setting row – a UUID, matching 'id' in the Prisma schema. This is a technical identifier not intended for external business use.

setting_key.description: Unique string identifier for the business policy/setting (e.g., 'currency', 'tax_region'). This is the main business-facing key, used in lookups and management. Uniqueness is enforced in the database.

setting_value.description: Arbitrary string value storing the operational parameter for this setting (may contain encoded JSON or plain string). Used by application logic to enforce configuration, e.g., the code for default currency, country, or qualitative threshold.

oneOf.description: Optional rich description clarifying the purpose, intended use, or documentation for this configuration row. This can be displayed in admin panels and audit logs. May be null if not documented.

description.description: Optional rich description clarifying the purpose, intended use, or documentation for this configuration row. This can be displayed in admin panels and audit logs. May be null if not documented.

created_at.description: Row creation timestamp in ISO 8601 format with timezone, for full audit traceability.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update (ISO 8601) to the business setting row, e.g., for value or description change.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp if the setting is retired or archived, or null if the record is currently active. Use to exclude soft-deleted settings from active API responses.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp if the setting is retired or archived, or null if the record is currently active. Use to exclude soft-deleted settings from active API responses.

IShoppingBusinessSetting.ICreate.description:
Schema for incoming request to create a new business setting in the platform-wide configuration table ('shopping_business_settings'). Only administrators may invoke creation. Required fields for creation are the unique business setting key and its corresponding value, plus (optionally) a human-readable description. Values are always stored as string data and must follow uniqueness/enforcement business logic.

This schema excludes system-managed fields like 'id', 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'deleted_at' – these are generated or managed by the backend. Values provided must be valid per business constraints, and if a duplicate key is detected, creation is rejected by the business logic. Used in endpoints for admin-level operational configuration setup; follows all field-level typing and nullability rules from the underlying Prisma schema.

setting_key.description: Unique business key for the new configuration row (e.g., 'currency', 'tax_region'). Must not duplicate an existing key, enforced by database unique constraint.

setting_value.description: Operational value to set for the business policy or configuration item. Any string is allowed per business logic; interpreted by downstream application components.

oneOf.description: Optional long-form documentation for this configuration entry. May include business rules, change log, or context for admin or compliance. Null if omitted.

description.description: Optional long-form documentation for this configuration entry. May include business rules, change log, or context for admin or compliance. Null if omitted.

setting_value.description: Arbitrary string data for the new setting value. This property holds the value to be applied for the business setting identified by setting_key. The string can be plain text or serialized JSON depending on the nature of the setting being modified (for example, currency code, country list, tax rules). See shopping_business_settings.setting_value in Prisma schema.

description.description: Optional description of this business setting. If provided, it documents the setting's business impact or intended usage. See shopping_business_settings.description in Prisma schema.

IShoppingBusinessSetting.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating an existing shopping business setting (shopping_business_settings). Used by platform admins to change system-wide configuration parameters that affect operational business logic (currency, regulatory policy, global flags, etc.). Only updates fields that are user-editable, in accordance with the shopping_business_settings table.

enum_domain.description: Domain of the status enum for filtering (e.g., 'order', 'payment'). Allows scoped lookup. Optional, maps to shopping_status_enums.enum_domain in Prisma schema.

status_code.description: Partial or exact status code match for filtering (case-insensitive). Optional, maps to shopping_status_enums.status_code in Prisma schema.

display_label.description: Partial or exact match on UI label for filtering. Optional, maps to shopping_status_enums.display_label. Supports full text search.

is_active.description: If true, only retrieves active status enums; false to only get inactive; omitted for both. Maps to shopping_status_enums.is_active in Prisma.

sort_by.description: Optional field name to use for result ordering (e.g., 'sort_order', 'created_at', 'display_label').

oneOf.description: Optional sort direction; must be 'asc' or 'desc'.
Optional sort direction; must be 'asc' or 'desc'.

sort_direction.description: Optional sort direction; must be 'asc' or 'desc'.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based index).

limit.description: Number of records to return per page. Maximum 100 per query, optional.

IShoppingStatusEnum.IRequest.description: Advanced search, filter, pagination, and ordering parameters for looking up platform-wide status enum codes (shopping_status_enums). Used in admin dashboards and code/config editors to locate and select status codes for business logic. Allows filtering by status domain, code, label, active flag, and supports sorting with pagination.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for this status enum entry in the shopping_status_enums table.

enum_domain.description: Domain/entity scope for this status enum (e.g., 'order', 'review', 'payment'). Used to categorize status codes by the relevant business entity or process.

status_code.description: Exact status code value for this enum within its domain (e.g., 'pending', 'paid', 'failed'). Must be unique within the enum_domain. Used in business logic and API flows.

display_label.description: Human-readable label for this status code, to be rendered in UIs or reports. May be localized as required.

sort_order.description: Integer value that determines display ordering in lists or dropdowns. Used for explicit sequencing in business workflows.

is_active.description: Indicates if this status enum is currently active and in use within the system's business logic. Inactive values are not shown in selection UI or validation.

description.description: Optional description or documentation for this enum value, providing operators or developers with business context and usage notes.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp for when this status enum was defined.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to this row (metadata, label, activation, etc).

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for this status enum definition. Set if the status enum is archived or removed from active business usage.

IShoppingStatusEnum.description: Status enum definition for shopping mall business domains such as orders, reviews, or payments. Represents one possible status code (with display label, active state, and metadata) for configuration-driven business state tracking. Linked to shopping_status_enums table. Used for validating, displaying, and managing allowable statuses in all business flows. Composite (enum_domain, status_code) key ensures domain-specific uniqueness. Includes audit and lifecycle metadata.

enum_domain.description: Domain/context for this status enum (e.g., 'order', 'review', 'payment'). Uniquely scopes the status_code and must correspond to a business entity using status codes.

status_code.description: Status code string identifying the discrete state for the enum within its domain (e.g., 'pending', 'paid'). Must be unique within the provided enum_domain.

display_label.description: UI or business display label for this status code. Shown in selectors, forms, and admin panels.

sort_order.description: Sort or ordering value for this enum when rendering in lists. Lower numbers come first.

is_active.description: True if this status code should be available for business workflows and user selection. False for legacy or archived codes.

description.description: Optional business context or documentation for this enum value, describing when and how it should be used.

IShoppingStatusEnum.ICreate.description: DTO for creating a new status enum in shopping_status_enums. Used by admin operations to add a new domain-specific status code, with its UI label, active state, and metadata. Composite (enum_domain, status_code) must remain unique within the system. Documentation and sort order control rendering/selection in administration/business logic UI flows.

display_label.description: Human-readable label for the status code as shown in UI or admin interfaces. Example: 'Payment Completed', 'Delivered', 'Failed'. Used for localization and business reporting. REQUIRED for relabeling.

sort_order.description: Ordering value for status codes, determines display sequencing in UIs. Must be integer. Lower values are prioritized first. Modify to reposition for dropdowns or logical workflows.

is_active.description: Flag that marks the enum code as currently enabled or not in business logic. true: actively used in workflows; false: deprecated or hidden from selection. Set to false to phase-out codes.

description.description: Optional business documentation, admin notes, or localization info about this status code. Not shown to end-users. May include localization keys, internal usage notes, or rationale for activation/deprecation.

IShoppingStatusEnum.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for shopping_status_enums. Used to change display label, ordering, active/inactive status, or description fields for an existing enum code (uniquely identified by enum_domain/status_code). Only metadata updatable; cannot modify underlying code/domain after creation. Used by admins during business logic updates.

tree_code.description: Filter by unique category tree code (e.g., 'main', 'brand'). Partial matching may be supported. OPTIONAL.

tree_name.description: Filter by display name of the tree using substring/partial matching. Case-insensitive. OPTIONAL.

created_from.description: Filter by trees created on or after this UTC datetime (ISO 8601). OPTIONAL.

created_to.description: Filter by trees created on or before this UTC datetime (ISO 8601). OPTIONAL.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based index). Optional, default=1.

limit.description: Results per page for pagination. Max 100, default=20.

IShoppingCategoryTree.description:
A category tree (taxonomy root) as defined in shopping_category_trees. Used for product and navigation classification. Includes identifiers, code, display name, optional description, creation/update/deletion timestamps.

Category trees define the top-level groupings for all categories (e.g., 'main', 'brands') and provide the context in which categories and hierarchical navigation trees exist. This model is referenced whenever products/categories are managed, created, or validated.

Maps exactly to the Prisma model `shopping_category_trees`.

tree_code.description: Globally unique business code for the new category tree (e.g., 'main', 'brand'), must match Prisma `tree_code`. Required for routing, APIs, and all category assignments. Unique constraint enforced by backend.

tree_name.description: English or official name for the new category tree, per `tree_name` in `shopping_category_trees`. Shown in admin and catalog configuration screens.

oneOf.description: Optional explanation of the business or operational context for this taxonomy, as per `description` column.

description.description: Optional explanation of the business or operational context for this taxonomy, as per `description` column.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp for the category tree. This should be set to the time of the update; it supports concurrency protection and audit. (See Prisma: shopping_category_trees.updated_at)

IShoppingCategory.IRequest.description: Advanced search and filter parameters for categories, including tree, parent/child, keyword, and pagination settings. Used in index operation for product category management.

id.description: Unique identifier for this category node. Universally unique per category and assigned by the database. Used by all operations for retrieval and parent/child relationships.

category_tree_id.description: Foreign key reference to the category tree (shopping_category_trees.id) this category belongs to. Determines the taxonomy or classification group for this category. Required.

category_name.description: Human-readable display name for the category. Used on catalog pages, navigation, and admin UI.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the category node was created. Used for auditing and ordering.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the last update to this record (rename, reorder, hierarchy changes, etc).

IShoppingCategory.description:
Category node in the shopping mall taxonomy hierarchy. Each node is part of a shopping_category_tree and may be nested under a parent (or be a root). Fields include unique business code, display name, parent reference, display order, and optional documentation. Soft-deletable, all changes timestamped for audit.

Relations:
- 'category_tree_id' points to the taxonomy/category tree (shopping_category_trees).
- 'parent_id' links to another category node if nested.
- Included 'sort_order' for sibling display and navigation control.
- 'deleted_at' used for soft-deletion/archiving.

For UI navigation, category trees, and product assignment/business logic.

category_tree_id.description: Foreign key (UUID) of the category tree (shopping_category_trees.id) to which this new category will belong. Required to specify the taxonomy for placement.

category_code.description: Unique and URL-friendly code (always lowercase) used to identify this category within the target tree. Must not duplicate any existing code in the same tree. Used for API lookups, navigation, and import/export flows.

category_name.description: Display name to show for the category in front-end navigation, admin UI, and selection widgets. Must be non-empty and meaningful for catalog users.

oneOf.description: (Optional) Parent category UUID if this category is nested under another. Set to null or omit for root-level nodes.

parent_id.description: Optional parent category node ID (UUID) if this category is a child of another node. Null or omitted for root categories. Used for hierarchical taxonomy setup.

sort_order.description: Integer value indicating where this node should appear among siblings under the same parent/root. Lower numbers are displayed first (e.g., 1 = top, 2, 3, ...).

oneOf.description: Optional, free-form documentation or display notes for the category node, used in admin interfaces.

description.description: Optional text documentation describing the business logic, purpose, or special display hints for this category node.

IShoppingCategory.ICreate.description: DTO for creating a new category node in a specific category tree. Used only by admin actors for catalog/taxonomy management. Requires unique category_code (per tree), display name, and sort_order. Supports optional parent_id for nesting within an existing category. Accepts optional documentation (description). Must match fields defined by 'shopping_categories' model (excluding system-managed IDs and timestamps, which are auto-generated). See business rules for unique constraint and parent/child logic.

category_name.description: New display name for the category node. Must remain unique among siblings in the same category tree and adhere to business rules outlined for catalog management (e.g., maximum length, no duplication within the same level). Updates the 'category_name' column in the shopping_categories table. When updating, platform validates uniqueness within the sibling set.

sort_order.description: Zero-based integer specifying the display position among sibling categories in its parent category node. Changing this reorders the node in catalog navigation and must not break business hierarchy constraints (e.g., sort_order uniqueness within siblings).

description.description: Optional human-readable description or managed documentation for the category node. When present, it should detail the business purpose, catalog context, or usage restrictions (e.g., restrictions on assignments to non-leaf categories). Used for admin and UI reference. If not provided, existing value is retained.

parent_id.description: Optional new parent category for this node (UUID from shopping_categories). Changing parent_id reassigns the node's location in the category tree. Must belong to the same category tree, not create cycles, and satisfy depth or hierarchy business rules. If omitted, the category remains at its current position.

IShoppingCategory.IUpdate.description:
Admin-side Data Transfer Object used to update an existing category node in a shopping mall category taxonomy (shopping_categories table). Fields supported for update include display name, sibling position sorting, admin/business description, and parent hierarchy reassignment, while all updates are subject to strict business rules:
- category_name must remain unique among siblings in the same tree
- sort_order must be a unique integer within its sibling group
- parent_id (if set) must remain in the same tree and not create cycles or violate hierarchy constraints
- Updates are thoroughly validated for hierarchical integrity, uniqueness, audit logging, and compliance with taxonomy governance policies
- Intended only for admin operations; all writes are fully audited
All property updates are validated to ensure conformity with business constraints for platform taxonomy management.

id.description: Unique identifier for the system log entry (primary key of shopping_system_logs table). Used for traceability and lookups in log diagnostics.

event_time.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) indicating when the log event occurred. Set by logging infrastructure at event generation. Critical for audit context and event sequencing.

log_level.description: Severity or log level for the event (examples include 'info', 'warn', 'error', 'fatal'). Reflects log significance for platform monitoring and support prioritization.

event_type.description: Category or type of the log event (e.g., 'system_init', 'migration', 'admin_action', 'error', 'scheduled_task'). Used for backend automation, diagnostics, and trace filtering.

event_source.description: Source/origin indicating the module, subsystem, or service generating this event (e.g., 'order_service', 'cron_worker'). Enables targeted investigation by platform teams.

message.description: Single-line summary or primary message for the log event, designed for operator readability in dashboards and alert feeds.

details.description: Optional extended metadata, details, or stack trace associated with the log event. May be JSON-encoded or raw text, based on subsystem conventions. Often contains diagnostic context, input parameters, or structured debugging information; should be used cautiously to avoid PII or secrets exposure.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the log row was persisted in the platform's durable store. ISO 8601 UTC, typically matches event_time but may differ for bulk ingestion or delayed writes.

IShoppingSystemLog.description:
Detailed record of a single system log entry, as registered in the shopping_system_logs table. Used for tracking all platform-level events, errors, migrations, and administrative actions in the e-commerce platform. All fields are intended for operator/admin/DevOps use:
- Field 'details' may contain JSON-encoded diagnostic metadata, stack trace, or business context, and should never expose plain secrets or sensitive PII; use care when ingesting and displaying
- All timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC for system-wide correlation
- Intended for backend observability, compliance, root-cause analysis, and performance investigations
Access to these records MUST be limited to authorized admin and operator roles due to possible exposure of sensitive system state and diagnostics. Used in audit trail reconstruction, security forensics, and business continuity reviews.

IShoppingCustomer.IRequest.description: Request parameters for filtered, paginated customer search. Used by admin/internal backends for customer list UIs and analytics. Supports standard search and paging logic. Does not directly expose restricted/sensitive customer fields.

email.description: Email address of the customer (used for login and contact). Uniquely identifies the customer. As per shopping_customers.email.

name.description: Customer's full display name, shown in order details and for personalization. From shopping_customers.name.

phone.description: Primary customer contact phone, formatted to local standard. Used for order notifications and delivery contacts. From shopping_customers.phone.
