IShoppingOrderStatusHistory.IRequest.description: Status history search/filter DTO for ShoppingOrder. Used to request paged status transition events with filter, sort, and range criteria for audit, transparency, or event debugging. All fields are optional, but both 'page' and 'limit' MUST always be included in API calls for consistent pagination and backward compatibility. Status filters reference allowed enum values for domain 'order' in shopping_status_enums. The 'actor' field allows searching by polymorphic actor (admin, seller, customer) and may correspond to an id or display name; actor type details may be supported by backend schema or event model. Non-index parameters are flexible; schema supports extension as needed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment attempt record, corresponding to the Prisma primary key. This property is a UUID string used to distinguish each discrete payment attempt logged for a given order and is indexed for audit, reconciliation, and reporting purposes.

shopping_order_id.description: Foreign key referencing the associated order (shopping_orders.id) for which this payment attempt is being recorded. Useful for linking the payment attempt with the business transaction, verifying context, and for order-based queries.

oneOf.description: External provider or gateway reference that uniquely identifies this payment attempt with a third-party payment processor or within the platform's own system. This field is typically assigned at the time of submission to the payment service (may be null until that time) and is globally unique. Important for dispute resolution and reconciliation with payment providers.

payment_reference.description: External provider or gateway reference that uniquely identifies this payment attempt with a third-party payment processor or within the platform's own system. This field is typically assigned at the time of submission to the payment service (may be null until that time) and is globally unique. Important for dispute resolution and reconciliation with payment providers.

attempt_status.description: Status code for this payment attempt (e.g., 'pending', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled'). Reflects the business and technical state of the payment event; used for reporting and recovery workflows.

amount.description: Total amount attempted to charge for this payment attempt, denominated in platform base currency. Used for reporting and reconciliation. Must match the expected order total for successful attempts.

attempted_at.description: Timestamp when the payment attempt was initiated. Used for audit, time window validation, and fraud detection.

oneOf.description: When the payment attempt finished (whether succeeded or failed/cancelled). Null if the attempt is still pending or in progress. Important for business logic regarding retrials, timeouts, and status transitions.

completed_at.description: When the payment attempt finished (whether succeeded or failed/cancelled). Null if the attempt is still pending or in progress. Important for business logic regarding retrials, timeouts, and status transitions.

IShoppingPaymentAttempt.description:
A detailed business object representing a single attempt to process payment for an order. Derived from the shopping_payment_attempts table, this schema provides all necessary context for tracking, reconciliation, and troubleshooting of payment events. It is used as a response body in endpoints where clients or administrators need to view status, audit logs, or investigate issues related to payment attempts. Sensitive external references should be included or masked based on actor permissions.

Links: shopping_orders, payment gateways, reporting subsystems.

IShoppingPaymentAttempt.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching payment attempts associated with a shopping order. Used in endpoints returning IPageIShoppingPaymentAttempt.

page.description: 1-based page number for paginated queries. Default: 1. Controls which set of payment attempts to retrieve.

limit.description: Maximum number of payment attempt items to return per page. Default may be 20; max enforced by business policy.

status.description: Optional filter; restricts results to payment attempts matching the specified 'attempt_status' (e.g., 'pending', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled').

payment_reference.description: Optional filter; retrieves payment attempt(s) by external provider or gateway reference. Used for tracing specific attempts by payment_reference value.

to_date.description: Optional end date/time (inclusive) as filter for latest creation time considered. ISO 8601 string.

IShoppingOrderFulfillment.IRequest.description: Request DTO used for paginated, filterable retrieval of order fulfillment records associated with a specific order. Accepts pagination fields and optional status/date-range filters. Used by customers, sellers, or admins to search, audit, or display order fulfillment events linked to an order. Filters map to business status states and order fulfillment date windows (see shopping_order_fulfillments table).

IShoppingOrderFulfillment.description:
Order fulfillment detail entity representing a specific shipment or delivery action for a customer order. This type directly maps to the `shopping_order_fulfillments` table in the Prisma schema, which tracks all fulfillment events for orders, including shipment, delivery, split shipment, or special logistics steps.

Each fulfillment record references the associated order line, the seller who fulfilled, the address from which fulfillment occurred, and includes status flags, fulfillment code for business traceability, timestamp of fulfillment event, fulfilled quantity, and optional logistics notes. It is a critical entity for shipment tracking, customer notifications, platform auditability, and reconciliation of split or partial shipments. The record is immutable once created, except for status updates, and is central to the order lifecycle in the shopping mall business flow.

References:
- `shopping_order_fulfillments`: Main fulfillment table (columns: id, shopping_order_line_id, shopping_seller_id, shopping_seller_address_id, fulfillment_code, quantity_fulfilled, fulfilled_at, status, note, created_at, updated_at)
- `shopping_order_lines`: Each order line fulfilled (reference by shopping_order_line_id)
- `shopping_sellers`: Business who fulfilled (reference by shopping_seller_id)
- `shopping_seller_addresses`: Shipping/warehouse address used (reference by shopping_seller_address_id)

Owned by all actors: customers, sellers, and admins (accessibility and security).

id.description: Unique identifier for this order fulfillment record (`shopping_order_fulfillments.id`).

shopping_order_line_id.description: Order line being fulfilled. Foreign key to shopping_order_lines.id.

shopping_seller_id.description: Seller who performed the fulfillment (`shopping_seller_id`). Foreign key to shopping_sellers.id.

shopping_seller_address_id.description: Warehouse or address from which fulfillment was dispatched. Foreign key to shopping_seller_addresses.id.

fulfillment_code.description: Globally unique business tracking code for this fulfillment event. Used for shipment tracking, audit, and customer notification (`fulfillment_code`).

quantity_fulfilled.description: Number of SKUs fulfilled in this event (`quantity_fulfilled`). Must be >= 1 and less than/equal to order line quantity.

fulfilled_at.description: Timestamp when the fulfillment (handoff to carrier or delivery) was completed (`fulfilled_at`). Required for tracking order lifecycle and customer notification.

status.description: Current fulfillment status (e.g. 'pending', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'). Business workflow field that tracks state transitions throughout the fulfillment process (`status`).

oneOf.description: Optional internal note or instructions associated with the fulfillment event (`note`). Used by sellers, fulfillment operations, or for platform audit trail.

note.description: Optional internal note or instructions associated with the fulfillment event (`note`). Used by sellers, fulfillment operations, or for platform audit trail.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the fulfillment record was created in the system (`created_at`).

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the last update to this fulfillment record occurred (`updated_at`).

IShoppingOrderAddress.IRequest.description:
DTO type for search, filtering, and pagination of order addresses (`shopping_order_addresses`) associated with a specific order. Used by customers, sellers, and admins to search, filter, and retrieve shipping and billing addresses for given orderCode. This schema supports filters by address type, recipient name, and paginated retrieval.

References:
- shopping_order_addresses table, with columns for address type, recipient, contact info, postal info, and order linkage.

Can support future extension for filtering on more address details or full text search.

type.description: Address type filter. Allows filtering by address class (e.g., 'shipping', 'billing'). Null to include all.

recipient_name.description: Filter for recipient name (full or partial match allowed).

page.description: Pagination parameter: select which page of results (1-based).

limit.description: Pagination parameter: number of results per page. Default 20, max 100.

oneOf.description: Generic search keyword for full-text address search (optional).

search.description: Generic search keyword for full-text address search (optional).

IShoppingOrderAddress.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order address for shopping orders. Linked to specific orders to record shipping or billing address at time of order. Based on the shopping_order_addresses Prisma model. Used for audit trails and summary views where full address context is needed without all details.

Includes key fields for delivery/tracking actor views. Soft delete determines historical preservation. Never includes linkage to user account outside of owning order for GDPR compliance.

All properties, types, and descriptions reflect the current Prisma schema definition. Do not add fields that do not exist in the schema.

id.description: Unique identifier for this order address record. Primary key on shopping_order_addresses.

shopping_order_id.description: Order this address is attached to. References shopping_orders.id.

recipient_name.description: Name of the delivery/billing recipient at this address.

base_address.description: Main address line or street address.

detail_address.description: Apt/suite or secondary details for address; nullable.

country.description: ISO or platform country string code for this address.

created_at.description: Address record creation timestamp.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp.

IShoppingRefundRequest.IRequest.description:
Filter and search DTO for retrieving paginated lists of refund, return, or cancellation requests in the shopping platform. Used by admin, customer, or seller users to filter requests based on business criteria as described in the business logic and API documentation.

All properties are optional and provide means to filter by request type, status, actor, associated order, time range, and support pagination/sorting. This type is not mapped directly to a single Prisma table but is designed to enable flexible, secure, and efficient refund queue management and audit reporting through search APIs. See functional requirements for details on permitted and expected business usage.

IShoppingRefundRequest.description:
Represents a single refund, return, or cancellation request initiated by a customer, seller, or admin for a specific order. This schema models the complete refund request entity as per the shopping_refund_requests table, encompassing all core properties that describe the lifecycle, business rationale, actor context, relations to order, status workflow, and attached documents.

Key relations are included for items involved in refund, associated order, initiating actor (customer, seller, or admin), status transitions, and audit trail for after-sales, dispute, and compliance workflows. The schema is designed to provide all data necessary for customer service, admin escalation, and business tracking use cases. Do not include any fields for actor ID input from the client in creation flows; those are always determined by authentication context. Sensitive information is visible only to authorized actors (requestor, order parties, platform admins).

id.description: Unique identifier for the refund request (UUID, shopping_refund_requests.id).

order.description: Summary information for the related order (shopping_orders table). Contains order_code, status, total_price, and minimal customer context. This object replaces shopping_order_id in the response DTO.

actor.description: Information about the actor (customer, seller, or admin) who initiated the request. Provides minimal summary fields for display and audit without exposing sensitive PII. This object replaces shopping_actor_id and actor_type.

oneOf.description: Business type of the request. Acceptable values: 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'. This reflects the high-level business action requested.
Business type of the request. Acceptable values: 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'. This reflects the high-level business action requested.
Business type of the request. Acceptable values: 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'. This reflects the high-level business action requested.

request_type.description: Business type of the request. Acceptable values: 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'. This reflects the high-level business action requested.

business_reason.description: Short, non-nullable business-provided reason for the refund, return, or cancellation request, such as 'item defective', 'ordered by mistake', or other structured value. (shopping_refund_requests.business_reason)

oneOf.description: Optionally, additional request metadata or rich business context provided for this request (maps to shopping_refund_requests.request_context). May be a serialized JSON string or plain text.

request_context.description: Optionally, additional request metadata or rich business context provided for this request (maps to shopping_refund_requests.request_context). May be a serialized JSON string or plain text.

status.description: Current workflow status of the refund request (e.g., 'pending', 'awaiting_approval', 'approved', 'declined', 'completed', 'escalated', etc.). See shopping_refund_requests.status.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the refund request was created (ISO 8601).

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the refund request was last updated (ISO 8601).

oneOf.description: Timestamp for soft deletion; null when active.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp for soft deletion; null when active.

items.description: Array of items (order lines) covered by this refund/return/cancellation request. Each item references a specific order line and indicates requested quantity.

attachments.description: List of supporting documents or files attached to the request or its items, referenced via IShoppingRefundAttachment.

status_histories.description: Chronological audit trail of all business status transitions for this refund request (see: shopping_refund_status_histories).

approvals.description: Formal records of approval or rejection events by admins/sellers regarding this refund request.

admin_overrides.description: If administrative override/escalation actions (by platform admin) exist for this request, they are listed here.

IShoppingRefundRequest.ICreate.description:
Request schema for creating a new refund, return, or cancellation request. This DTO captures all client-submitted data needed to initiate a new refund request, as per the shopping_refund_requests table. The client must specify the related order, the type of request, the business reason, and the list of order lines/items to be covered by the request. Attachments for supporting evidence may also be provided.

Do not accept any fields for actor identity (such as actor_id or actor_type); these are determined by authenticated session context and enforced by the backend based on the user's role (customer, seller, admin). All validation on order eligibility and item context is enforced by business logic in the backend service.

shopping_order_id.description: Identifier of the order for which this refund request is being made (maps to shopping_orders.id).

oneOf.description: Business type for the request: must be one of 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'.
Business type for the request: must be one of 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'.
Business type for the request: must be one of 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'.

request_type.description: Business type for the request: must be one of 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'.

business_reason.description: Short, required business-provided reason for the refund/return request. E.g., 'item defective', 'ordered by mistake', etc. (maps to shopping_refund_requests.business_reason).

oneOf.description: Optional: additional structured business context or metadata for the request, such as JSON-encoded details, free-form comments, or rationale for the refund.

request_context.description: Optional: additional structured business context or metadata for the request, such as JSON-encoded details, free-form comments, or rationale for the refund.

items.description: List of specific order lines/items to include in the refund request. Each entry specifies which order line and how many units are being requested for refund. (maps to shopping_refund_request_items)

attachments.description: Array of supporting documents or files to attach to the refund request or its items.

id.description: Unique identifier for the order record in the system, directly sourced from shopping_orders.id. Used for referencing this order in all business workflows, including dashboard operations, analytics, refunds, and shipping.

order_code.description: Globally unique, human-readable code referencing this order (shopping_orders.order_code). Used in customer-facing screens, order management, and business communications.

total_price.description: Total monetary value for all items in the order, as computed from order lines (shopping_orders.total_price). Used in payment settlement and analytics.

status.description: Current status of the order (shopping_orders.status), such as pending, paid, fulfilled, or canceled. Business logic values reference the platform status enums for order workflow management.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this order was created (shopping_orders.created_at). Used for lifecycle tracking and order history timelines.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the latest modification to this order (shopping_orders.updated_at). Used to monitor workflow transitions.

customer.description: Summary information for the customer who placed this order. Derived from shopping_customer_id FK in shopping_orders; includes reference fields for linking to full customer profile or audit context.

IShoppingOrder.ISummary.description: Comprehensive order summary DTO for order listings, user dashboards, admin panels, or analytics interfaces. This schema summarizes core order identity and state, with a reference to the ordering customer, and is used throughout business flows to provide lightweight but complete context for each order. Intended for quick display, search, or reporting scenarios, and as a backbone of order-related business process navigation. All properties map directly to the shopping_orders table. Full order details (lines, addresses, payments) are found in the corresponding detail DTO.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for this specific refund request item (UUID, global scope).

shopping_refund_request_id.description: Parent refund request ID (UUID). References shopping_refund_requests.id. Represents the refund case to which this item belongs.

shopping_order_id.description: Target order ID (UUID). References shopping_orders.id. Indicates which order this refunded item is part of.

shopping_order_line_id.description: Specific order line (SKU) being refunded. References shopping_order_lines.id. Traceable to customer order line for audit, eligibility and SKU context.

quantity.description: Number of units from the underlying order line being requested for refund/return/cancellation. Must be ≥1 and ≤ original order line quantity. Enforced by business validation.

item_business_reason.description: Optional. If present, business reason for refund/return on this item (e.g., defect, wrong item, changed mind). String; overrides parent reason. Nullable: can be null if not provided.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the refund item request was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_at.description: Timestamp for last modification of this item (ISO 8601, UTC).

attachments.description: Array of evidence or supporting attachments (photos, docs, etc) for this refund request item. Attachment entries reference files in storage.

IShoppingRefundRequestItem.description: Represents an individual refund request item, which links a specific order line (SKU in an order) to a refund/return/cancellation process. Used for per-item tracking under a parent refund request. Follows the structure of the shopping_refund_request_items table. Includes all business context for traceability, audit, and business logic. Each refund request item is associated with a specific order, order line, and potentially a SKU; contains quantity for refund, optional business reason, and allows retrieval of any associated attachments (evidence, photos, etc). Timestamps support full lifecycle and audit trails. This component is a critical part of the refund management flow, enabling per-item adjustments, approval, and documentation.

shopping_order_id.description: Target order ID (UUID). Must match parent refund request order; references shopping_orders.id.

shopping_order_line_id.description: Specific order line (shopping_order_lines.id) being added/requested for refund. Must not already exist as a refund item for this refund request.

quantity.description: Number of units from the order line being requested for refund/return/cancellation. Must be ≥1 and ≤ the order line's available quantity.

item_business_reason.description: Optional: Per-item reason or details for this refund/return/cancellation claim. If present, overrides parent reason.

attachments.description: Optional: Attachments (e.g. photos, invoices, evidence) supporting this item. Each must reference an existing file asset and is used solely for evidence/context. Note: The API enforces that only new refund request items (never duplicates) can be added to a given refund request; each order line may be included at most once per refund request.

IShoppingRefundRequestItem.ICreate.description: Request body for creating (adding) a refund request item to an open refund/return/cancellation case. Used to submit a new line item for a refund, specifying the exact order line (SKU), quantity, optional business reason, and any supporting attachment files (if provided). Input is validated for uniqueness—duplicate refund request items for the same order line within a single refund request are not allowed. Attachments are for evidentiary or business context only and do not affect order line or business logic directly; they serve to document and support the claim. Typically used by the customer actor, but admin or seller may also add on escalation. Attachments, if provided, use the IShoppingRefundAttachment.ICreate variant.

id.description: Unique identifier for the order line, matching the 'id' field in 'shopping_order_lines' table of the database. Each entry represents a distinct item purchased as part of the order.

shopping_order_id.description: ID of the parent order (from 'shopping_orders.id') to which this line belongs.

sku.description: Summary information about the purchased SKU/product variant for this order line. Transforms the foreign key 'shopping_sku_id' to IShoppingSKU.ISummary to provide business and display context, following platform best practices for summary relations.

seller.description: Minimal summary of the seller who owns this order line's product/SKU. Replaces the raw 'shopping_seller_id' FK. Contains seller id and display name for context.

quantity.description: Number of units for this SKU purchased in the order line.

unit_price.description: Final per-unit price for the SKU in this order line, after tax/discounts.

status.description: Current fulfillment status of this item (e.g., 'pending', 'shipped', 'delivered').

created_at.description: Order line creation timestamp.

updated_at.description: Most recent update timestamp for this order line.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp if this order line has been logically deleted. Null if still active. Used for audit, compliance, and visibility of historical order data.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp if this order line has been logically deleted. Null if still active. Used for audit, compliance, and visibility of historical order data.

IShoppingOrderLine.ISummary.description: Order Line Summary DTO. Represents a concise summary of a single item (SKU) ordered by a customer, including context for SKU (product variant), seller (ISeller.ISummary), order, quantity, and price. Used for list views and embedding in higher-level order or split summaries. Implements correct API context references by transforming all relation FKs to summary objects for improved context. Maps directly to the order line records in the database, but with summary transformation for all business context fields. Includes 'deleted_at' for soft-delete/audit-trail consistency.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the refund attachment as the primary key in shopping_refund_attachments.

shopping_refund_request_id.description: UUID referencing the parent refund request (shopping_refund_requests.id) to which this attachment belongs.

shopping_refund_request_item_id.description: Optional UUID referencing the specific refund request item (shopping_refund_request_items.id) this attachment is associated with. Null if not linked to any item.

attachment_file_id.description: UUID linking to the actual file asset stored in the attachment store (shopping_product_images.id or other).

attachment_type.description: Type or category of this attachment (e.g., 'evidence', 'photo', 'invoice', etc.).

description.description: Optional human-readable description or purpose of the attachment. Can provide business/context info.

uploaded_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp specifying when the attachment was uploaded.

file_uri.description: Direct URI for the file asset. Can be used for preview/download by authorized actors. Required for all attachments referencing physical files (e.g., images, documents, videos). Must be an externally accessible URI, such as a presigned S3 or CDN link, as used in other attachment schemas across the platform.

file_type.description: File MIME/media type (e.g., 'image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf', etc.). Required for policy-compliant upload/management and for correct file format validation by consumers. Must conform to platform/business-allowed types listed in corresponding requirements for refund attachments.

file_size.description: File size in bytes, used to enforce allowed upload limits and client-side validation. Required for all attachments and enforced by business logic both on creation and download/management flows.

IShoppingRefundAttachment.description: Metadata and access information for a single attachment file associated with a refund, return, or cancellation request. This schema corresponds to the shopping_refund_attachments table and now includes file_uri, file_type, and file_size fields, which are required for API clients and business logic to manage and consume attached evidence or documentation files in refund processes. Attachment_file_id is a reference to the stored file asset, while file_uri provides the direct download or preview link, file_type describes the MIME/media format, and file_size aids in validation and enforcement of limits. These additions bring the DTO in line with OpenAPI completeness and maintain consistency with all other attachment/file schemas across platform resource domains.

attachment_file_id.description: UUID referencing the already-uploaded file asset. Must exist in attachment file storage (e.g., shopping_product_images.id) at the time this record is created.

attachment_type.description: Type/category of the attachment (e.g., 'evidence', 'photo', 'invoice'). Business logic may restrict valid values depending on refund process.

description.description: Optional free-form description/purpose for the attachment being submitted. May be used for internal notes, filename, context, etc.

shopping_refund_request_item_id.description: (Optional) UUID of the refund request item (shopping_refund_request_items.id) if the attachment is linked to a specific refunded line/SKU. Null if linked only to the overall request.

file_uri.description: Direct URI for the uploaded attachment file (e.g., presigned CDN link or persistent storage URL). Required for creation for access and compliance verification.

file_type.description: File MIME/media type (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf', etc.). Required for business and platform validation.

file_size.description: Size of the attachment file in bytes. Required for upload validation and enforcement.

IShoppingRefundAttachment.ICreate.description: Request schema for creating a new refund attachment record, as used when associating an uploaded file with a refund, return, or cancellation request. In addition to file asset id and business type, the DTO now requires file_uri (direct file link), file_type (MIME/media type), and file_size (in bytes). These fields must be submitted by clients and are used by the backend to enforce file/content policy, business upload limits, and to expose files to authorized consumers. This aligns the refund attachment creation process with platform standards for all other attachment and resource file schemas.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the refund status history entry. Primary key of the shopping_refund_status_histories table.

shopping_refund_request_id.description: Foreign key referencing the parent refund request (shopping_refund_requests.id).

shopping_actor_id.description: UUID of the actor (customer, seller, or admin) who performed this transition. Resolved using actor_type.

oneOf.description: Type of actor who initiated the status change. Enumerated as 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.
Type of actor who initiated the status change. Enumerated as 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.
Type of actor who initiated the status change. Enumerated as 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.

actor_type.description: Type of actor who initiated the status change. Enumerated as 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.

previous_status.description: Business status value prior to this transition. Reflects the refund/return process state before this event (e.g., 'pending', 'awaiting_approval', etc.).

new_status.description: Business status value after this transition. Reflects the refund/return process state after this event.

timestamp.description: Timestamp when the status transition occurred (ISO 8601 format, UTC).

change_context.description: Optional notes, rationale, or business context for the transition. Provided by the actor during status change. May include system-supplied or user-provided explanations.

IShoppingRefundStatusHistory.description: Detailed representation of a single status change event (transition) in a refund/return/cancellation workflow. Mirrors a row from shopping_refund_status_histories. Includes auditing of who performed the change, what states were involved, when it occurred, and why (as context). Used to support audit trails, compliance reviews, and workflow tracking in refund operations.

IShoppingRefundApproval.description:
Entity DTO for a refund approval/rejection action as recorded in the shopping_refund_approvals table. Each instance represents a single approval or rejection (by admin or seller) tied to a refund process and logs all critical audit fields.

This schema provides full transparency in business logic chains around refund status transitions. It contains references to the parent refund request, the specific status change being approved, the actor (admin or seller), the type of approval action taken (approved/rejected), an optional audit note, and when the approval was recorded. 

This type is returned in detail endpoints (GET /shopping/admin/refunds/{refundRequestId}/approvals/{approvalId}) and forms the core unit of business audit, compliance, and regulatory reporting for the refund workflow.

Sensitive fields such as actor_id MAY be filtered at the API layer for non-admin consumers. No fields are writable by clients except in restricted admin contexts.

id.description: Primary key of the approval record (UUID), unique within shopping_refund_approvals table.

shopping_refund_request_id.description: ID of the parent refund request (shopping_refund_requests.id).

shopping_refund_status_history_id.description: ID of the associated refund status history entry (shopping_refund_status_histories.id) this approval/rejection refers to.

actor_type.description: Type of actor performing the action. Must be either 'admin' or 'seller'. Use enum values from business rules.

actor_id.description: UUID of the actor (admin or seller) who performed the approval/rejection. (MAY be filtered for privacy/context compliance.)

action.description: Type of approval action taken on the refund: 'approved' or 'rejected'. (Use enum values only.)

note.description: Optional human-readable note provided as rationale for the approval/rejection. May be null or omitted if no rationale given.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the approval/rejection was recorded (ISO 8601, UTC).

id.description: Primary key for the admin refund override action (UUID).

shopping_refund_request_id.description: UUID of the refund request this override was performed against (foreign key to shopping_refund_requests.id).

shopping_admin_id.description: UUID of the admin actor executing this override (foreign key to shopping_admins.id).

override_type.description: Exact override action taken by the admin, e.g., 'force_accept', 'force_reject', 'reassign', or other business-constant types as defined in platform policy.

reason.description: Short, business-facing description explaining why the override action was performed (required field).

detailed_context.description: Additional context about the override, such as business/legal notes or serialized extra info (nullable string).

created_at.description: Timestamp when this override action was issued (ISO 8601 UTC format, required).

IShoppingRefundAdminOverride.description: Detailed schema for a single refund admin override record (shopping_refund_admin_overrides table), including admin, type, and business context. Used for retrieval and audit-logging purposes.

business_reason.description: Short business-provided reason for the refund, return, or cancellation request. May be updated by authorized actors during the request lifecycle. This maps to the 'business_reason' column on the shopping_refund_requests table. Used for conveying the core rationale to sellers or platform admins.

status.description: Current business status of the refund request after the update. Only permissible status transitions are accepted, appropriate to the actor role and the request type. This reflects workflow progress or resolution stages, e.g., 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'completed', and must conform to status code values defined elsewhere in the business logic. This updates the 'status' column on the shopping_refund_requests table.

request_context.description: Optional additional structured context or metadata associated with the request (may be JSON-encoded as string), e.g., explaining supporting evidence or request detail to help adjudicate the claim. This field is nullable and maps to the 'request_context' column.

IShoppingRefundRequest.IUpdate.description: DTO for updating an existing refund, return, or cancellation request in the shopping_refund_requests table. Allows authorized actors (customer/seller/admin) to modify fields such as the core business_reason, status (within permitted transitions), and additional request_context metadata. Does NOT permit changing foundational fields such as request_type, actor identity, or linked order. Field updates are always subject to business logic, status transition rules, and audit requirements. This interface is mapped to the updatable columns of the Prisma shopping_refund_requests model and is linked by the 'x-autobe-prisma-schema' tag for compiler validation. All fields are optional and only supplied fields will be updated in the underlying record.

page.description: Page number for paginated results (1-based). Defaults to 1 if unspecified. Used for navigating large sets of refund request items linked to a given refund.

limit.description: Number of items to include per page of results. Typical business defaults are 20, and this value should not exceed platform constraints (e.g., 100 max) for performance and DoS safety.

sku_code.description: Optionally filter or search refund items by the SKU code referenced. Filters the result set to items related to a specific SKU. This should match the 'sku_code' associated on linked order lines.

order_line_id.description: Optionally filter by a specific order line item associated with the refund request. Useful for narrowing the scope to a particular item in the order.

status.description: Optional filter by status of the individual refund request items (e.g., pending, approved, rejected, completed). Should map to business status codes supported on refund items.

IShoppingRefundRequestItem.IRequest.description: DTO for advanced search, filtering, and pagination of refund request items associated with a given refund request. Supplies criteria such as page number, page size, SKU code, order line ID, and per-item status for precise result set control. Used in list/retrieval endpoints to help actors (customer, seller, admin) navigate/refine large refund claims or itemized cases. This type does not map directly to a single Prisma table, but query context is always scoped to the parent refundRequestId in the endpoint path or parameter. Optional fields only, and no x-autobe-prisma-schema is included because this DTO models search/filter parameters, not an updatable row.

quantity.description: Number of units in the order line requested for refund/return/cancellation (must be ≥1, ≤ order line quantity). Set during an update to adjust how many units are included in the amended refund item. Constraints are enforced to prevent exceeding allowed order line quantity or using zero/negative values.

item_business_reason.description: Optional item-specific business reason for requesting refund. Supersedes the parent's reason if set. Used by customers or admins to clarify or correct the reason for partial claim or item amendment. Not required unless business rules demand item-level rationale.

IShoppingRefundRequestItem.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for refund request item modification.

This schema represents the updatable properties for a single refund (return/cancellation) request item, aligned with the `shopping_refund_request_items` table in the database. It allows for the adjustment of the claim quantity and the business reason for the refund at the item level. Fields correspond to those tracked in the underlying table, supporting business processes such as amendment of quantity or reason prior to approval or administrative escalation. Authorization is enforced so only the request submitter or an admin can amend details while the parent refund is editable. All business rule constraints—such as not exceeding original order line quantity, and not being permitted to update closed requests—are handled at the service layer.

page.description: Page number for pagination (optional, defaults to 1 if omitted). Used to control paginated retrieval of attachment records. Must be positive if supplied.

limit.description: Page size—the number of attachment records to return per page. Optional; defaults to system policy (commonly 20). Must be between 1 and 100, per business limits.

attachment_type.description: Filter for specific attachment type (e.g., 'evidence', 'photo', 'invoice'). Optional—used to narrow search to specific kinds of evidence, if desired. Only attachments matching this type will be returned if supplied.

uploaded_after.description: ISO8601 date-time. Optional lower bound filter—only attachments uploaded after this timestamp are included in the result set.

uploaded_before.description: ISO8601 date-time. Optional upper bound filter—only attachments uploaded before this timestamp are included in the result set.

keyword.description: Optional keyword or search query to filter by description, file name, or text fields in the attachment metadata.

IShoppingRefundAttachment.IRequest.description: Attachment listing/filter request for refund evidence. This schema enables advanced search or pagination over the set of attachments for a given refund request, as used in audit, moderation, or evidence review business flows. All properties are optional—supplying none requests the entire set. Filters support type, date, and keyword-based narrowing. Pagination is supported by 'page' and 'limit'. Proper usage supports business compliance with complex refund/return documentation and investigation requirements.

page.description: Page number for results pagination (starting from 1). Used to navigate through batched status history records. Optional; default is 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of refund status history entries per page. Supports controlling page size for large histories (default 20, max 100).

oneOf.description: Optional filter to restrict status histories to those performed by a specific actor type. Valid values: 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.
Optional filter to restrict status histories to those performed by a specific actor type. Valid values: 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.
Optional filter to restrict status histories to those performed by a specific actor type. Valid values: 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.

actor_type.description: Optional filter to restrict status histories to those performed by a specific actor type. Valid values: 'customer', 'seller', or 'admin'.

status_transition.description: Optional filter to return only histories with a specific status transition (e.g., 'pending_to_approved'). The specific format or enumeration depends on the application's state logic.

from_date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Optionally filter status history entries that occurred after this date/time. Used for range queries.

to_date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Optionally filter entries before or up to this date/time. Used with from_date for bounding the time range.

oneOf.description: Sort order for results by occurred_at timestamp. Allowed values: 'asc' (oldest-to-newest), 'desc' (newest-to-oldest). Defaults to 'asc'.
Sort order for results by occurred_at timestamp. Allowed values: 'asc' (oldest-to-newest), 'desc' (newest-to-oldest). Defaults to 'asc'.

sort.description: Sort order for results by occurred_at timestamp. Allowed values: 'asc' (oldest-to-newest), 'desc' (newest-to-oldest). Defaults to 'asc'.

IShoppingRefundStatusHistory.IRequest.description: Request query criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating the status history of a refund request. Enables scoped listing of status transitions, optionally filtered by actor type, status changes, and time ranges. Follows strict pagination and filtering conventions. Used for endpoints exposing audit trails of refund/return/cancellation workflows.

IShoppingRefundApproval.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching, filtering, and paginating the approval/rejection records related to a specific refund request. This DTO is used to retrieve a list of approval actions (admin or seller) performed on refund status transitions, supporting audit, compliance, and business analytics.

This schema includes standard paginated list controls (page, pageSize), allows searching by actor type, actor id, approval action (approved/rejected), approval status, and optional filtering by time window or note. Referenced directly by PATCH endpoints for customer/seller/admin approval list search operations.

All filter fields are optional, allowing precise query construction. The schema is designed to map to the core filtering/query model of the shopping_refund_approvals Prisma table. DO NOT include any actor_id fields that would allow user identity spoofing – all identity information must come from JWT/session context for customers or sellers.

page.description: Current pagination page number (1-based). Default: 1.

pageSize.description: Number of approval records per page. Default: 20. Max: 100.

actor_type.description: Optional filter for actor type (e.g. 'admin','seller'). Filters returned approvals by the role of the actor who made the decision. If omitted, returns all actors.

actor_id.description: Optional filter for the specific actor who performed the approval/rejection. If omitted, disables actor-based filtering.

action.description: Optional filter for approval action type (e.g. 'approved','rejected'). Returns only approvals with the requested action status.

fromCreatedAt.description: Optional filter for approvals created at or after this ISO 8601 datetime.

toCreatedAt.description: Optional filter for approvals created before this ISO 8601 datetime.

has_note.description: Optional filter to return only approvals with a non-empty note field (if true), or those with an empty/null note (if false).

search.description: Optional search query term to filter override actions by reason, admin, or context. Full-text search supported across main string fields.

override_type.description: If set, filters results to only include admin override actions matching this type (e.g., 'force_accept', 'force_reject', 'reassign', case-sensitive business constants).

admin_id.description: If set, restricts results to overrides performed by this admin. Uses admin unique UUID.

from.description: Start of the date/time range filter. Only overrides created at or after this datetime will be returned, if provided (ISO 8601 format).

to.description: End of the date/time range filter. Only overrides created at or before this datetime will be returned, if provided (ISO 8601 format).

oneOf.description: Sort column to order results. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'override_type'. Defaults to 'created_at'.
Sort column to order results. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'override_type'. Defaults to 'created_at'.

sort_by.description: Sort column to order results. Allowed values: 'created_at', 'override_type'. Defaults to 'created_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. Only accepts 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'desc'.
Sort direction. Only accepts 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'desc'.

sort_order.description: Sort direction. Only accepts 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'desc'.

page.description: 1-based page number to retrieve (pagination). Default is 1.

page_size.description: Number of records per page (pagination). Minimum: 1, Maximum: 100. Defaults to 20.

IShoppingRefundAdminOverride.IRequest.description: Request parameters for searching, filtering, sorting, and paginating admin refund override actions for a given refund request. Fields correspond to common filtering criteria (search term, override type, admin actor, time range), result sorting, and pagination—support compliance and regulatory audit scenarios.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin override record.

shopping_refund_request_id.description: The unique identifier for the refund request that was overridden by admin.

shopping_admin_id.description: The unique identifier of the admin who performed the override.

override_type.description: The type of override action performed by the admin, such as 'force_accept', 'force_reject', 'reassign', etc.

reason.description: Required business or legal reason for this override action.

detailed_context.description: Optional field containing additional business, legal, or technical context regarding the override event. May be JSON-encoded or free-form text.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the override action was recorded, in ISO 8601 format.

IShoppingRefundAdminOverride.ISummary.description: Summary of an administrative override operation on a refund request, performed by a platform admin. This type outlines the action taken (such as force-approve or force-reject), reason, context, actor, and timestamp for audit and business reporting. For full details and relational constraints, refer to the shopping_refund_admin_overrides Prisma schema. Commonly used in admin audit trails, refund escalation logs, and compliance workflows.

page.description: The page number for pagination of shipment search results. Required for paginated output.

limit.description: Maximum number of shipments returned per page (default: 20, max: 100).

order_code.description: Filter by (partial or exact) order code related to a shipment. Optional, for admin or seller logistic search.

seller_id.description: Filter for shipments belonging to this seller (UUID). Optional, used mostly for admin search. Sellers will search their own shipments.

status.description: Filter by shipment status (e.g., pending, packed, in_transit, delivered, canceled, returned, or any status registered in the status enum table).

carrier_company.description: Filter by shipping/courier company (e.g., FedEx, CJ대한통운). Optional. Matches any company if omitted.

scheduled_dispatch_at_from.description: Earliest scheduled dispatch date for shipments to search for (ISO8601). Optional.

scheduled_dispatch_at_to.description: Latest scheduled dispatch date for shipments to search for (ISO8601). Optional.

dispatched_at_from.description: Earliest actual dispatched date to filter shipments by (ISO8601). Optional.

dispatched_at_to.description: Latest actual dispatched date to filter shipments by (ISO8601). Optional.

created_at_from.description: Earliest creation date for the shipment record. Optional.

created_at_to.description: Latest creation date for the shipment record. Optional.
