sort_field.description: Which field to use for sort ordering (created_at, updated_at, scheduled_dispatch_at, dispatched_at, delivered_at).

oneOf.description: Order of sorting. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Order of sorting. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Order of sorting. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

IShoppingShipment.IRequest.description: Shipment search filter and pagination for advanced shipment query. Allows searching by order, status, carrier company, various shipment timestamps, and paginated navigation. Used for both admin and seller advanced shipment search interfaces.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shipment record (UUID, primary key from shopping_shipments).

code.description: Business-meaningful unique shipment code (e.g. SHPT-2025-0100). Used externally in shipping, logistics, and as lookup reference. Mapped from Prisma shopping_shipments.code.

shopping_order_id.description: UUID of the underlying order being shipped. Foreign key to shopping_orders.

shopping_seller_id.description: UUID of the seller responsible for this shipment. Foreign key to shopping_sellers.

status.description: Shipment's current state (e.g., pending, packed, in_transit, delivered, canceled, returned). Must match status values registered in the status enum table. Mapped from Prisma shopping_shipments.status.

carrier_company.description: Shipping/courier company in charge of delivery (e.g., FedEx, CJ대한통운, UPS). Business relevant field.

carrier_service_type.description: The specific courier service used for this shipment (e.g., overnight, express, standard). Optional field. Maps to carrier_service_type in Prisma; can be null.

scheduled_dispatch_at.description: Planned shipping/dispatched date/time (ISO 8601) for warehouse logistics, nullable if not scheduled. Maps to scheduled_dispatch_at in prisma.

dispatched_at.description: Date/time when the shipment was physically handed over to courier. May be null if not yet dispatched.

delivered_at.description: Timestamp when shipment was fully delivered (via courier or customer confirmation). Null if not yet delivered.

canceled_at.description: Timestamp if shipment was canceled. Null if not yet canceled.

created_at.description: When the shipment entity was created (ISO8601).

updated_at.description: When the shipment entity was last updated (ISO8601).

shopping_order.description: Summary of the original order being fulfilled in this shipment. Maps to child fields from shopping_orders. Used as a reference object for business context.

shopping_seller.description: Summary info about the owning seller responsible for the shipment (identity, display name, business contact, etc).

packages.description: Physical packages included in this shipment, as arrays of IShoppingShipmentPackage.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp for soft deletion of the shipment entity. Null if not deleted. NOT exposed in normal responses, but present for admin audit/detail.

IShoppingShipment.description: Detailed description of a shipment as registered in the shopping mall platform, including key shipment logistics, owner context, and physical package breakdown. Fully audit-traceable, comprehensive for logistic tracking, and mapped to shopping_shipments schema.

IShoppingShipmentPackage.description:
Represents a single physical package within a shipment, as defined by the shopping_shipment_packages model in the shopping mall platform. This entity provides comprehensive details for operational tracking, audit compliance, customer notifications, exception handling (such as lost/damaged packages), and integration with external carrier workflows. Each package is uniquely identified and scoped to its parent shipment, and contains all logistical details, including sequence within a split shipment, business/warehouse label, registered tracking number (carrier-facing), package weight/dimensions for cost and customs, and full audit trail of creation, updates, and exception events.

This DTO is used for shipment detail display, package-level tracking and troubleshooting, customer service support scenarios (lost, delayed, or damaged packages), and compliance-driven reporting. It supports real-time tracking integration and fits directly into user- and seller-facing shipment UIs, as well as admin/fulfillment dashboards. The schema follows enterprise documentation practices and all fields include operational context and usage guidance.

id.description: Unique identifier for this shipment package (UUID). Primary key in the shopping_shipment_packages table. Used for audit and cross-referencing in all systems.

shopping_shipment_id.description: Foreign key linking this package to its parent shipment (shopping_shipments.id). Uniquely associates each package to a shipment event for multi-package or split-shipment orders. Critical for mapping package events back to the overall order fulfillment flow.

sequence.description: Zero-based order/index of this package within the parent shipment. Used for operational display, tracking status updates, automated sorting, and reconciliation of split shipments (e.g., for multi-box deliveries or partial fulfillments).

package_label.description: Business/warehouse label assigned to this package for internal and carrier logistics. Serves as a unique reference within the shipment for physical picking/packing, customer inquiries, and shipment audit. Typically printed/scanned as a barcode or QR code. Required for end-to-end package differentiation.

tracking_number.description: Courier/vendor-provided tracking number for this package. This value is used by both customers and logistics/seller teams to observe real-time carrier status, external shipment events, and for troubleshooting lost or delayed packages. The tracking number must be unique per shipment and is critical for global tracking portal integrations.

package_weight_grams.description: Declared or measured total weight of the package in grams. Used for compliance with shipping regulations, cost determination, and customs declarations. Downstream systems and carriers may use this data for correct routing and cost calculation.

length_cm.description: Length of the package (in centimeters). Required for fulfillment routing and cost estimation. All physical package dimensions are critical for carriers, third-party integration, and audit tracking.

width_cm.description: Width of the package (in centimeters). Used for cost, logistics, and fulfillment processing.

height_cm.description: Height of the package (in centimeters). Used for correct carrier calculations and internal packaging constraints.

status.description: Current package-level business status. Permitted values include: 'pending', 'ready', 'shipped', 'in_transit', 'delivered', 'lost', 'damaged', and others permitted by the status enum logic for package delivery lifecycle. This value reflects not only logistical events but also compliance and after-sales scenarios (e.g., exceptions for lost/damaged claims).

delivered_at.description: Timestamp when the package was confirmed delivered by courier scan or customer acknowledgment. Null until package is officially delivered (fully closed). Used for compliance, customer notification, and escalated support. Formatted as ISO 8601 date-time string.

lost_at.description: If the package status transitions to 'lost' (e.g., missing/lost in transit by carrier), this field is set to the recorded date/time. Null unless package is officially declared lost. Used for refunds, compliance, and claim management. ISO 8601 date-time or null.

damaged_at.description: If a package is marked as damaged (e.g., by carrier scan or upon customer receipt), this is the time the event was logged. Null otherwise. Important for after-sales support, insurance claims, and operational flagging. ISO 8601 date-time or null.

created_at.description: Package record creation timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601 format). Used for package lifecycle audit trail and shipment event replay.

updated_at.description: Most recent update to any package property or status (UTC, ISO 8601 format). Used for operational and compliance auditing.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp if this package record is removed/historically archived for audit/compliance purposes. Null unless record has been archived or removed from business flow. ISO 8601 date-time or null.

IShoppingShipment.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for shopping_shipments table. Used for updating mutable logistics and business attributes of a shipment as an authorized actor (admin or seller). Fields include only those eligible for in-place modification; core shipment identifiers (code, id, order association) are not present and must NOT be supplied. This DTO supports business workflows for real-time shipment lifecycle state management, operational compliance (e.g., dispatch/delivery/cancellation audit), and tight integration with external carriers and fulfillment partners. Any update to status or associated timestamps must adhere to platform-defined business rules regarding valid state transitions, role-based permissions, and audit trail requirements. For each updatable timestamp, supply an explicit ISO 8601 string or null value. Only allowable field changes are processed; extraneous or immutable properties are ignored or rejected. All updates are stringent for audit and transactional compliance.

status.description: Status of the shipment (e.g., 'pending', 'packed', 'in_transit', 'delivered', 'canceled', 'returned'). Allowed values must correspond to status enums configured in the platform and reflect only valid state transitions per business logic. Mutability is restricted by fulfillment progression and permission model.

carrier_company.description: Business display name of the shipping/courier company responsible for the shipment (e.g., 'FedEx', 'CJ대한통운'). May be updated to reflect assignment or carrier change as shipment progresses. Carrier data must be valid per platform integration rules.

carrier_service_type.description: Optional field specifying the logistics service type (e.g., 'overnight', 'express', 'standard') for this shipment. Nullable if not used in the business scenario. Should adhere to service types defined in external carrier integrations and platform business rules. Can be updated for re-routing or service upgrades.

scheduled_dispatch_at.description: The planned/scheduled dispatch (warehouse exit) timestamp for the shipment, used for fulfillment planning and customer notification. Must be an ISO 8601 date-time string or null. Can be set/adjusted as business needs or logistics context change.

dispatched_at.description: The timestamp when the shipment was actually dispatched (handed off to courier for delivery). Must be an ISO 8601 date-time string or null. Reflects the operational moment of physical goods exit from the warehouse/fulfillment center. Only settable when status allows by business logic.

delivered_at.description: The timestamp when the shipment was delivered (courier or customer confirmation). Updates final state and triggers delivery completion flows (such as enabling post-sale review, returns, etc). Must be an ISO 8601 date-time string or null. Platform logic controls when this value can be changed.

canceled_at.description: If the shipment is canceled, this is the time that status officially changed. Set by workflow automation or explicit admin/seller action. Used for post-cancellation fulfillment and refund processing. Must be ISO 8601 date-time string or null.

status.description: Filter for package status (pending, ready, shipped, in_transit, delivered, lost, damaged). See shopping_shipment_packages.status.

tracking_number.description: Exact or partial match filter for the package tracking number. See shopping_shipment_packages.tracking_number.

package_label.description: Filter for the package label (carrier/warehouse-internal reference). See shopping_shipment_packages.package_label.

sequence.description: Exact match filter for package sequence/order in the shipment.

delivered_at_from.description: Start date range filter for delivered_at timestamp. ISO 8601.

delivered_at_to.description: End date range filter for delivered_at timestamp. ISO 8601.

sort_by.description: Sort field for result set (sequence, delivered_at, status).

oneOf.description: Sort direction (ascending or descending).
Sort direction (ascending or descending).

sort_order.description: Sort direction (ascending or descending).

page.description: Page number for paginated result sets. Must be >= 1.

limit.description: Maximum results per page. Platform default is 20, maximum is 100.

IShoppingShipmentPackage.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and filtering shipment packages (shopping_shipment_packages). Allows filtering by status, tracking number, label, sequence, delivered_at range, and supports sort, pagination. Used in the context of a single shipment to retrieve a paginated list of its packages. All fields are optional and can be combined for advanced querying.

IShoppingShipmentTracking.IRequest.description: Filtering, sorting, and pagination query DTO for shipment package tracking event search.

tracking_source.description: Optional tracking source filter: limits results to only tracking entries from a particular source (e.g. 'courier_api', 'warehouse_scan', 'manual'). String value defined by business or carrier system.

status.description: Optional tracking status filter. Restricts returned tracking/events to those with matching current status (e.g. 'in_transit', 'delivered', 'delayed', 'lost'). Business/courier-defined status types.

event_start_at.description: Optional event window filter (start). Only events at or after this timestamp will be included. Set as ISO-8601 string or null.

event_end_at.description: Optional event window filter (end). Only events up to or before this timestamp (inclusive) will be included. Set as ISO-8601 string or null.

sort_by.description: Optional field to control returned result sort order (e.g. 'event_time', 'status', 'created_at'). If omitted, default backend sort is applied.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for search results, either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.
Sort direction for search results, either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

sort_order.description: Sort direction for search results, either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

page.description: Requested page number for pagination (1-based, defaults to 1 if not provided).

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page (default: 20, max: 100).

id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying the tracking instance. Corresponds to the shopping_shipment_trackings.id column.

shopping_shipment_package_id.description: Foreign key referencing the shipment package for this tracking record (shopping_shipment_packages.id).

tracking_source.description: Describes the source of tracking data (e.g., 'courier_api', 'warehouse_scan', 'customer_report').

external_tracking_id.description: Unique tracking reference from the external carrier/courier or null if not available.

status.description: Most recently reported status from this tracking instance (e.g., 'in_transit', 'delivered', 'delayed', etc.).

status_detail.description: Most recent detailed description from the latest tracking status, may be raw text from carrier or the system.

last_update_at.description: Timestamp of last update from carrier, scan, or system ingestion.

estimated_delivery_at.description: Estimated delivery timestamp, if provided by the courier or computed by the system.

created_at.description: Tracking row created UTC timestamp.

updated_at.description: Last modification UTC timestamp for this tracking instance.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp, present if the tracking instance was deleted.

IShoppingShipmentTracking.description: A tracking instance for a shipment package, describing the latest carrier status, source, and traceability. Provides status, detail, estimated delivery, and reference back to the external carrier system if any. Derived from shopping_shipment_trackings in the Prisma schema.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based).

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return per page.

search.description: Full-text search filter for event codes, statuses, or location.

sort_by.description: Sorting field ('event_time', 'event_code', 'location').

oneOf.description: Sort direction: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').
Sort direction: ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

event_code.description: Filter for a specific event code (e.g., 'DELIVERED', 'IN_TRANSIT', etc.).

location.description: Filter tracking events by carrier-reported location.

to_datetime.description: Filter events up to this datetime (inclusive).

IShoppingShipmentTrackingEvent.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and paginating shipment tracking events. Used for PATCH /trackings/{trackingSource}/events endpoints. Parameters are based on filtering shipping event history by code, location, and time range.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the shipment tracking event as defined in shopping_shipment_tracking_events.id.

shopping_shipment_tracking_id.description: FK. Linked tracking instance which this event belongs to (shopping_shipment_tracking_events.shopping_shipment_tracking_id).

event_time.description: Timestamp when the tracking event occurred (such as carrier scan, status transition, or callback receipt). May differ from system ingestion/creation time—for example, carrier updates can arrive delayed or batch-synced. Value is always UTC.

event_code.description: Carrier or platform event code: e.g., 'DELIVERED', 'IN_TRANSIT', 'OUT_FOR_DELIVERY', 'ARRIVED_AT_HUB', or a business-defined custom code for system-internal events. Values are not strictly enumerated but are typically standardized by major carriers and correspond to carrier reference documentation.

location.description: Location at which the event occurred, such as a city name, warehouse, or geo tag. Supplied by the carrier/platform if available. Null if the carrier/platform does not provide location information for the event—API consumers should always check for presence.

raw_status.description: Unprocessed, full raw status message from the tracking provider or external system. Used for display, debugging, integration troubleshooting, or complete audit. May not be suitable for direct end-user presentation and often contains carrier-specific phrasing or codes.

external_ref.description: URL or string identifier provided by the external tracking system (such as a tracking link, scan ID, or other carrier event reference). Nullable if unavailable from the provider. Acts as a cross-reference to external tracking data sources.

ingested_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when this event was first recorded/received by the platform from the carrier/courier, which may differ from event_time if updates are delayed or fetched in batch. Always auto-generated by the system API layer.

created_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when this tracking event record was created in the platform database. Usually matches ingested_at, but may differ in rare migration or correction scenarios.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp: non-null (ISO 8601) only if this tracking event was deleted (typically for GDPR or audit correction). Normally null for active events. Never physically deleted from audit logs.

IShoppingShipmentTrackingEvent.description:
Represents a single log/audit event within the platform shipment tracking process—such as a status change, scan, or callback from an external courier/carrier or system event. 

Each record details the occurrence (event_time), the event type (event_code), raw message received (raw_status), optional location and external references, and audit/ingestion timings for precise traceability and operational compliance. Tracking events are append-only, never modified, and used to build a full timeline of package delivery. Integration consumers should consult carrier documentation for typical event_code values, and always validate for null/empty location and references on less-instrumented carriers.

IShoppingReview.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating shopping reviews. Used in endpoints to retrieve lists of customer product reviews by admin, seller, or customer roles. Supports full-text comment keyword search, star rating filtering, review state masking, date interval queries, author or SKU filtering, and advanced sort/pagination options. All filters apply to the shopping_reviews table, which associates each review with a customer, SKU, and order line.

Properties are tailored for analytics, moderation, and reporting, including permissions context. Pagination properties are required to ensure robust, scalable queries. Optional filter granularity and sorts enable deep admin and business analytics. Does not include business-internal fields (password, sensitive actor linkage). Implements strict type and usage matching with the database schema for search and filter use cases.

page.description: The page number to retrieve (starts from 1). Enables paginated retrieval of reviews. Must be a positive integer.

limit.description: The maximum number of reviews to return per page. Default and hard maximum are business configurable, typically between 20 and 100. Used for large paginated result sets.

oneOf.description: Sort field. Options are: created_at, updated_at, rating, or state. Determines review order for reporting, moderation, UI, or export. If not provided, defaults to created_at descending.
Sort field. Options are: created_at, updated_at, rating, or state. Determines review order for reporting, moderation, UI, or export. If not provided, defaults to created_at descending.
Sort field. Options are: created_at, updated_at, rating, or state. Determines review order for reporting, moderation, UI, or export. If not provided, defaults to created_at descending.
Sort field. Options are: created_at, updated_at, rating, or state. Determines review order for reporting, moderation, UI, or export. If not provided, defaults to created_at descending.

sort_by.description: Sort field. Options are: created_at, updated_at, rating, or state. Determines review order for reporting, moderation, UI, or export. If not provided, defaults to created_at descending.

oneOf.description: Sort direction/order (ascending/descending). Must be 'asc' or 'desc'. Combined with sort_by for deterministic ordering.
Sort direction/order (ascending/descending). Must be 'asc' or 'desc'. Combined with sort_by for deterministic ordering.

sort_order.description: Sort direction/order (ascending/descending). Must be 'asc' or 'desc'. Combined with sort_by for deterministic ordering.

query.description: Full-text keyword search against the review comment and other indexed fields. Enables UI search bar, phrase or word queries, or admin search. Uses trgm index for efficient fuzzy/partial text matching. Optional.

oneOf.description: Filter for review visibility or moderation state. Only values available in the status_code column of the shopping_status_enums table under the 'review' domain are allowed. Useful for moderation analytics, reporting, and filtering forbidden content.

Filter for review visibility or moderation state. Only values available in the status_code column of the shopping_status_enums table under the 'review' domain are allowed. Useful for moderation analytics, reporting, and filtering forbidden content.

Filter for review visibility or moderation state. Only values available in the status_code column of the shopping_status_enums table under the 'review' domain are allowed. Useful for moderation analytics, reporting, and filtering forbidden content.

Filter for review visibility or moderation state. Only values available in the status_code column of the shopping_status_enums table under the 'review' domain are allowed. Useful for moderation analytics, reporting, and filtering forbidden content.

review_state.description: Filter for review visibility or moderation state. Only values available in the status_code column of the shopping_status_enums table under the 'review' domain are allowed. Useful for moderation analytics, reporting, and filtering forbidden content.

star_rating.description: Filter for reviews by exact star rating (between 1 and 5). Supports reporting, aggregation, or targeted search by review rating. Optional; omit/null means no star filter.

customer_id.description: Filter for reviews authored by a specific customer (UUID). Must match shopping_customers.id. Used for profile pages, admin queries, or self-service dashboards.

sku_id.description: Filter for reviews linked to a specific SKU (UUID). Must match shopping_skus.id. Enables product detail view analytics, seller quality reporting, or customer review lookup.

order_line_id.description: Filter for reviews tied to a specific order line (UUID). Used to enforce eligibility, identify review context, or for fraud moderation auditing.

created_at_from.description: Start of creation timestamp range for queries. Follows ISO 8601 date-time (UTC, eg. 2024-05-20T15:04:05Z). Used for historical analytics, time window search, or bulk export.

created_at_to.description: End of creation timestamp range for queries. Follows ISO 8601 date-time (UTC). Records created before or at this instant are included.

include_deleted.description: If set true, includes reviews that are soft deleted (deleted_at != null). Default is false (do not show deleted reviews). Only visible to admin roles. Use with caution due to volume/PII.

include_pending.description: If true, includes reviews that are pending moderation (state = 'pending_moderation'). Default is false (do not show pending moderation). Only privileged actors (admin, seller) can enable.

IShoppingReview.description:
Full detail view of a customer product review submitted in the shopping mall platform. This type is equivalent to a full record from the shopping_reviews table, uniquely associating a customer (reviewer), SKU, and order line for each review. Includes all fields needed for detailed display, moderation, audit, and response features. Integrates associated customer summary, SKU summary, attachments, and relevant audit/moderation data. Does not expose sensitive account or internal system fields.

Field semantics align strictly to business review policies, and actors can only request reviews where their permissions are satisfied.

All relations are expressed with summary or core types using $ref. This type is the main data contract for displaying or moderating individual reviews, supporting business logic for moderation workflows, abuse reporting flows, and audit data reconstruction. Properties use strict typing, referential integrity, and full documentation referencing the associated Prisma schema.

Review content is always subject to moderation and business eligibility, and only reviews matching permissions/context may be returned per role.

id.description: Review unique identifier (UUID, PK in shopping_reviews).

customer.description: Summary of the reviewing customer, derived from shopping_customers. Contains minimal display and audit info for privacy.

sku.description: Summary of the reviewed SKU, referencing shopping_skus. For product display, rating rollups, and context. Id, code, name only.

order_line_id.description: FK to shopping_order_lines.id indicating which order line this review is for. Used for business eligibility and context.

rating.description: Star rating value given by customer (1–5). Enforced at write and on update per business policy. Aggregated in analytics.

comment.description: Text review content (comment). Required for all reviews. Must be between 10 and 2000 characters, as enforced in business policy.

oneOf.description: Current visibility/moderation state for this review (e.g., visible, pending_moderation, removed, under_review). Must align with shopping_status_enums under the 'review' domain.
Current visibility/moderation state for this review (e.g., visible, pending_moderation, removed, under_review). Must align with shopping_status_enums under the 'review' domain.
Current visibility/moderation state for this review (e.g., visible, pending_moderation, removed, under_review). Must align with shopping_status_enums under the 'review' domain.
Current visibility/moderation state for this review (e.g., visible, pending_moderation, removed, under_review). Must align with shopping_status_enums under the 'review' domain.

state.description: Current visibility/moderation state for this review (e.g., visible, pending_moderation, removed, under_review). Must align with shopping_status_enums under the 'review' domain.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the review was created. ISO 8601 UTC.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for most recent update to the review. ISO 8601 UTC.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp, if this review has been removed. Nullable; present if deleted, absent/null if active.

attachments.description: List of URIs for all file/image/video attachments linked to this review. Data comes from shopping_review_attachments, limited to configured max count and file size policies. Attachments may be images or videos, each with uri, mimetype, and size.

moderation.description: Moderation/audit logs for this review (admin actions). Derived from shopping_review_moderations table. Each entry includes admin summary, action type, action timestamp, optional reason/comment.

abuse_reports.description: Abuse reports (open or resolved) for this review, as submitted by other actors. Derived from shopping_review_abuse_reports. Each entry includes reporting actor summary, category, report state, and comment.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the attachment in the shopping_review_attachments table.

shopping_review_id.description: ID of the parent review to which this attachment belongs. Foreign key to shopping_reviews.id.

file_uri.description: Storage URI or URL for the attachment file. This is typically an externally accessible path pointing to cloud or server storage, e.g., S3 or CDN URL.

file_size.description: Attachment file size in bytes, as recorded at upload time.

created_at.description: Attachment creation timestamp, in RFC3339/ISO 8601 UTC format.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete marker for the attachment. Null unless the attachment is deleted (in moderation, user request, or business rule).

shopping_review.description: Summary info for the parent review object (attachment context). Used for embedding minimal review data in attachment lists.

IShoppingReviewAttachment.description: Attachment file entity for review photos, videos, or documents submitted by customers on product/SKU reviews. Each record is a row in shopping_review_attachments. Includes externally stored file URI, MIME type, upload timestamp, and soft-delete status.  For use in review details, moderation, and compliance views. Only returned for attachments not marked as soft-deleted unless include_deleted is explicitly true in search. Ownership and review context enforced by API authorization. See the shopping_review_attachments model in Prisma schema for full mapping.

IShoppingReviewModeration.description: Represents a moderation action log entry for a specific review in the shopping mall platform. This schema captures all metadata associated with a moderation decision, including the action type (approved, removed, restored, flagged, edited, etc.), rationale provided by the moderator, moderator identity, review reference, and precise timestamps. It enables audit, compliance, and legal transparency for all admin decisions regarding user-submitted reviews, in conformance with platform business requirements and audit traceability. Each moderation is uniquely associated with a review and an admin moderator, ensuring full context for regulatory and business reporting.  This object is created only by admins, and all fields have been aligned to match the shopping_review_moderations Prisma model. Timestamps, relationships, and rationale fields are documented for maximum resolution during dispute or appeal review workflows.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of this moderation log entry, mapping to the shopping_review_moderations.id column.

shopping_review_id.description: Target review for this moderation log. Foreign key referencing shopping_reviews.id. Indicates which review this moderation action was applied to.

moderator_admin_id.description: Reference to the admin moderator who performed or logged this action. Foreign key to shopping_admins.id. Used for internal traceability, appeals, and compliance.

action.description: Type of moderation action applied to the review. Typical values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited', etc. Reflects the core decision or intervention performed on the review. Corresponds directly to the 'action' column in shopping_review_moderations.

oneOf.description: Optional free-text reason or rationale provided by the moderator/admin for the action taken. This is audit and compliance-facing; helps to justify moderation outcomes in appeals/workflow scenarios. Maps to reason column (nullable).

reason.description: Optional free-text reason or rationale provided by the moderator/admin for the action taken. This is audit and compliance-facing; helps to justify moderation outcomes in appeals/workflow scenarios. Maps to reason column (nullable).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the moderation record was created. Maps to created_at in shopping_review_moderations.

IShoppingReviewAbuseReport.description:
Entity representing a customer-filed abuse report against a product review for moderation and audit purposes. Each abuse report records the reporter (customer), associated review, abuse type (such as 'spam', 'hate_speech', etc.), optional comments, moderation state, and full audit information. Used in reporting, moderation, and administrative audit workflows. Based on shopping_review_abuse_reports table constraints. Personally identifying information about the reporter is masked or restricted to admins as per the business requirements. The entity ensures traceability and integrity for all abuse moderation processes, with soft-deletion support for compliance.

Business rules enforce that only customers can create reports, only one report per customer per review is allowed, and only authorized actors (platform moderators, admins) can view all report details. All changes are fully audited.

id.description: Unique identifier for this abuse report (UUID, PK in shopping_review_abuse_reports).

shopping_review_id.description: ID of the reviewed product review to which this abuse report is attached. Foreign key to shopping_reviews.id.

reporter_customer_id.description: UUID of the customer who reported abuse. May be masked or anonymized per business rules. FK to shopping_customers.id.

report_type.description: Type of abuse flagged by reporter. Business code as per platform abuse categories, e.g. 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'off_topic'. Enum-constrained, see business documentation.

comment.description: Optional comment or explanation from reporter describing the abuse. Business constraints typically limit to 500-2000 characters. Nullable.

state.description: Current moderation state of the abuse report. E.g., 'open', 'processed', 'dismissed', 'removed'. Business rules limit how state can change.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when this abuse report was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the report was last changed.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp if this abuse report was removed by business or moderation workflow. Null if active.

IShoppingReview.ICreate.title: IShoppingReview.ICreate
IShoppingReview.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new review for a specific SKU in an order. This DTO enables an authenticated customer to submit a review for a purchased item, including a star rating (1–5), a required textual comment (10–2000 characters), and optional attachments (image/video references, up to 5 files under 5MB each).

Security restrictions: review authorship (customer, SKU, order line) is validated on the server from JWT context—no author/customer/order_line IDs are accepted directly in the payload. Attachments are passed as URIs and are handled separately via attachment subsystem.

Maps directly to the shopping_reviews table except for actor and order line context which must be inferred from authentication and path parameters.

References original Prisma schema: shopping_reviews.

shopping_sku_id.description: Target SKU to be reviewed. Must reference an SKU the authenticated customer has purchased and received via a delivered order line. This value is strictly validated server-side against order delivery state and review eligibility. Maps to shopping_reviews.shopping_sku_id.

shopping_order_line_id.description: Order line corresponding to the purchased SKU being reviewed. Ensures only delivered SKUs from this specific order are eligible for review. The provided order line must correspond to a delivered item purchased by the authenticated customer. Maps to shopping_reviews.shopping_order_line_id.

rating.description: The star rating assigned, from 1 (worst) to 5 (best). Must be an integer and comply with business rule. This is required for aggregation in reviews. Maps to shopping_reviews.rating.

comment.description: Written review text, between 10 and 2,000 characters. May be subject to moderation or banned keyword checks. Maps to shopping_reviews.comment.

attachments.description: Optional array of file/image/video attachments. Each attachment must comply with type/size constraints (generally <5MB and approved file formats). Attachments are referenced through URI and are associated separately in the attachments subsystem. This field is mapped to shopping_review_attachments via association.

IShoppingReview.IUpdate.title: IShoppingReview.IUpdate
IShoppingReview.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing review for a specific SKU in an order. This DTO enables the original customer author to change the rating, comment, and attachments for their review, but only within the editable window (by default, 7 days after submission). Attempts to update after the period will be blocked with error code 'REVIEW_EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED.'

Security restrictions: Edits are strictly limited to the review author, and only for reviews in 'visible' or 'pending_moderation' state. Actor and review eligibility is determined via JWT and path parameters—no direct review or customer IDs are accepted in the payload.

Maps directly to the shopping_reviews table for updatable fields (rating, comment, attachments). Attachments are updated transactionally through the attachment subsystem.

References original Prisma schema: shopping_reviews.

rating.description: New star rating (1–5) to update the review. If omitted, rating remains unchanged. Maps to shopping_reviews.rating.

comment.description: Updated review body text (10–2000 chars). If omitted, comment remains unchanged. Maps to shopping_reviews.comment.

attachments.description: Optional array of new or replacement attachments (image/video files). Each must pass constraints (size, type). If omitted, attachments remain unchanged. If provided, will replace all previous attachments. Managed via attachment subsystem, not directly in shopping_reviews.

file_uri.description: Storage URI or URL for the attachment file. Must be an externally uploaded and accessible URL for image, video, or document. (JPEG, PNG, MP4, PDF, etc.)

file_type.description: Mime/media type of the attachment (e.g., image/png, image/jpeg, video/mp4, application/pdf, etc.). Must match file content type.

file_size.description: Attachment file size in bytes. Must not exceed business limit (typically 5MB).

IShoppingReviewAttachment.ICreate.description: DTO for registering a new review attachment. Used as requestBody in POST /shopping/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/attachments or /shopping/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/attachments. Represents metadata for a file (already uploaded externally) to be attached to a customer/product review. The attachment must conform to business validation: permitted type, size, and per-review attachment count. This interface does not include review or actor IDs, which are inferred from context and auth. Maps directly to shopping_review_attachments table except for foreign keys, which are determined server-side.

file_type.description: Attachment file type filter (e.g., 'image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'video/mp4'). Supports filtering to specific MIME types allowed by platform business policy. Consult API documentation for the list of permitted file types. Optional: if omitted, returns all supported MIME types.

upload_date_from.description: Retrieve attachments uploaded on or after this ISO 8601 date-time (inclusive). Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. Optional: if omitted, all upload dates are included.

upload_date_to.description: Retrieve attachments uploaded before or on this ISO 8601 date-time (inclusive). Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. Optional: if omitted, all upload dates are included.

include_deleted.description: If true, include soft-deleted (logically removed) attachment files in the result set for audit or moderation purposes. Default is false; deleted attachments are excluded unless this flag is set. Optional.

page.description: Result page number for paginated responses, starting from 1. Optional; default is 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Maximum number of attachments to retrieve per page. Optional; default is 20, maximum allowed is 100. Returns fewer results if not enough data are present.

IShoppingReviewAttachment.IRequest.description: Filtering, search, and pagination parameters for listing shopping_review_attachments (review file/image/video attachments). Allows filtering by MIME type (see file_type), upload dates (upload_date_from/to, ISO 8601), soft deletion state, and paginated response control. Only officially permitted file types based on business rules may be queried. Used as the request body for batch attachment listing endpoints in moderation/feedback workflows. All fields are optional: omitting all returns all undeleted attachments for the review in descending creation order.

IShoppingReviewAttachment.IReviewSummary.description: Summary of the parent review for a review attachment. Used when displaying context information in attachment listing or moderation UIs. This summary DTO is non-recursive: it contains only minimal review context, and never includes child arrays or nested composition. Business logic may restrict or mask text for soft-deleted reviews.

id.description: Unique identifier of the review, as shopping_reviews.id.

shopping_customer_id.description: ID of the customer who authored the review (shopping_reviews.shopping_customer_id).

shopping_sku_id.description: ID of the SKU being reviewed (shopping_reviews.shopping_sku_id).

rating.description: Rating value (number of stars, 1 to 5) as assigned by the reviewer in shopping_reviews.rating.

comment.description: Short textual review (10-2000 characters) visible in summary/context lists. For soft-deleted reviews, this may be masked per policy.

state.description: Moderation or workflow state for this review; e.g., 'visible', 'pending_moderation', 'removed', or 'under_review'. See platform enums for allowed values.

created_at.description: Timestamp of review creation (ISO 8601, shopping_reviews.created_at).

page.description: Page of results to retrieve for moderation log pagination. Must be 1 or greater. Default is 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page. Business policy may enforce a cap (usually 20-100).

oneOf.description: Column to sort moderation logs by. Allowed values are 'created_at' for sorting by timestamp (default) and 'action' for moderation action type.
Column to sort moderation logs by. Allowed values are 'created_at' for sorting by timestamp (default) and 'action' for moderation action type.

sort_by.description: Column to sort moderation logs by. Allowed values are 'created_at' for sorting by timestamp (default) and 'action' for moderation action type.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction for logs. Allowed values: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).
Sort order direction for logs. Allowed values: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

sort_direction.description: Sort order direction for logs. Allowed values: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

moderator_admin_id.description: Optional filter to restrict moderation log search to actions performed by a specific admin (moderator), by admin UUID (RFC 4122).

oneOf.description: Optional filter for moderation action type; only results with this action type are included in the response. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'.
Optional filter for moderation action type; only results with this action type are included in the response. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'.
Optional filter for moderation action type; only results with this action type are included in the response. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'.
Optional filter for moderation action type; only results with this action type are included in the response. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'.
Optional filter for moderation action type; only results with this action type are included in the response. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'.

action.description: Optional filter for moderation action type; only results with this action type are included in the response. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'.

date_from.description: Filter: Start ISO8601 date-time (UTC). Only moderation log records created at or after this time are included.

date_to.description: Filter: End ISO8601 date-time (UTC). Only moderation logs created at or before this time are included.

IShoppingReviewModeration.IRequest.description: DTO for searching and filtering review moderation logs (shopping_review_moderations). Used as request body for admin API to list moderation events. Supports paginated search and enum-controlled filters: moderator (admin), action (business enum: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'), sort columns ('created_at', 'action'), and sort directions ('asc', 'desc'), and ISO8601 UTC date window. Descriptions provide explicit allowed values and workflow details.

IShoppingReviewModeration.ICreate.description: Data required to create a new moderation log entry for a specific review, representing an admin's decision/intervention. Used by platform admins to formally record a moderation action, rationale, and acting moderator (injected server-side, not sent in body). The action property is restricted to these allowed values: ['approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited']. The reason field is optional/null, but rationale is required for removals and flags and is always recommended for audit. Chronological index and identity are set by backend.

oneOf.description: The moderation action to perform, corresponding to the intended admin/moderator decision. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'. Required. Only these are allowed to ensure moderation workflow and audit history integrity.

The moderation action to perform, corresponding to the intended admin/moderator decision. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'. Required. Only these are allowed to ensure moderation workflow and audit history integrity.

The moderation action to perform, corresponding to the intended admin/moderator decision. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'. Required. Only these are allowed to ensure moderation workflow and audit history integrity.

The moderation action to perform, corresponding to the intended admin/moderator decision. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'. Required. Only these are allowed to ensure moderation workflow and audit history integrity.

The moderation action to perform, corresponding to the intended admin/moderator decision. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'. Required. Only these are allowed to ensure moderation workflow and audit history integrity.

action.description: The moderation action to perform, corresponding to the intended admin/moderator decision. Allowed values: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited'. Required. Only these are allowed to ensure moderation workflow and audit history integrity.

oneOf.description: Optional rationale for this moderation action. Human-readable comment from the admin as to the justification or business rule for the moderation intervention. Required for removals and flags; always recommended for full audit trace. Nullable.

reason.description: Optional rationale for this moderation action. Human-readable comment from the admin as to the justification or business rule for the moderation intervention. Required for removals and flags; always recommended for full audit trace. Nullable.

IShoppingReviewAbuseReport.IRequest.description: Request parameters for listing or filtering review abuse reports. Used in search, moderation, and listing endpoints for abuse reports. Refer to shopping_review_abuse_reports table for field constraints. Provides advanced filtering and pagination for large numbers of abuse reports associated with reviews. All filtering options adhere to business workflow described in abuse report requirements.

search.description: Keyword for searching within abuse report comments or report types (case-insensitive, partial match allowed). Optional.

type.description: Type of abuse reported. This matches the business code defined in shopping_review_abuse_reports.report_type. Typical values: 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'off_topic', etc. Optional, use business constraints/enum for allowed values.

state.description: Current moderation state of the abuse report, as in shopping_review_abuse_reports.state. Typical values: 'open', 'processed', 'dismissed', 'removed'. Optional.

reporter_customer_id.description: Filter by the reporting customer's UUID. Optional. Only admins can use this field to retrieve reports by specific reporter.

created_from.description: Filter to only abuse reports created after this timestamp (inclusive, ISO 8601). Optional.

created_to.description: Filter to only abuse reports created before this timestamp (inclusive, ISO 8601). Optional.

page.description: The result page number (one-based). Defaults to 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Number of results per page, default 20. 1-100 allowed.

oneOf.description: Which column to sort results by. Acceptable values: 'created_at', 'state'.
Which column to sort results by. Acceptable values: 'created_at', 'state'.

sort_by.description: Which column to sort results by. Acceptable values: 'created_at', 'state'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for results, either ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').
Sort direction for results, either ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

sort_order.description: Sort direction for results, either ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

report_type.description: Type/category of abuse reported (e.g., 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'off_topic'). This must match allowed business-defined codes for abuse reports.

comment.description: Optional textual explanation or evidence for the report. May contain additional user context or clarification regarding the abuse report.

IShoppingReviewAbuseReport.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new review abuse report. Used by customers to report abuse on a specific review. The report_type field specifies the kind of abuse claimed (e.g. 'spam', 'hate_speech', etc.) and is required based on business rules. The comment field is optional, allowing the user to elaborate on the circumstances or reason. See the shopping_review_abuse_reports Prisma schema for additional context.

report_type.description: Updated report type (abuse category for this report), e.g., 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'off_topic'. Only updateable if allowed by workflow and business logic.

comment.description: Optional user comment to update or clarify the previous report. May be required depending on workflow and business rules.

IShoppingReviewAbuseReport.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating an existing review abuse report. Allows editing the abuse report type and comment, if business and moderation rules permit. May not be allowed in all report workflow states (e.g., if already resolved or dismissed).

id.description: Unique identifier for the review and rating aggregate. References the primary key in shopping_review_rating_aggregates.

shopping_sku_id.description: The UUID of the SKU for these review statistics (shopping_skus.id).

shopping_product_id.description: The parent product's UUID for SKU-level aggregation (shopping_products.id).

review_count.description: Total number of visible, eligible customer reviews for this SKU, as last aggregated.

average_rating.description: SKU-level average rating (1.0–5.0 scale, one decimal precision).

product_review_count.description: Sum of review counts across all SKUs for this product.

product_average_rating.description: Weighted product-wide average rating, across all SKUs (one decimal precision).

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this aggregate was last updated/refreshed.

IShoppingReviewRatingAggregate.description: Aggregated review and rating summary statistics for a SKU and its parent product, materialized from customer reviews by business batch logic. Used for catalog, product page, and ranking/scoring display. Derived from shopping_review_rating_aggregates table; includes SKU- and product-level metrics for customer-facing and search/sort UIs.

page.description: Page number for paginated audit log results (starts at 1).

limit.description: Page size for number of records per page. Default: 20. Platform maximum: 200.

category.description: Optional filter for audit log records by category. Matches shopping_audit_logs.category.

event_type.description: Optional filter for specific audit log event type (e.g., 'ADMIN_SUSPEND_SELLER').

admin_id.description: Optional: filter events performed by a specific admin (actor). UUID reference to shopping_admins.id.

seller_id.description: Optional: filter events for/affecting a specific seller. UUID reference to shopping_sellers.id.

customer_id.description: Optional: filter events for/affecting a customer. UUID reference to shopping_customers.id.

date_from.description: ISO 8601 lower bound for created_at filtering (datetime inclusive).

date_to.description: ISO 8601 upper bound for created_at filtering (datetime inclusive).

description_q.description: Optional: substring/keyword full-text filter for description field (shopping_audit_logs.description).

IShoppingAuditLog.IRequest.description: Request DTO for shopping audit log paging and advanced filtering. Allows admins to search audit logs by actor (admin/seller/customer), category, event_type, time range, or keyword(s) in description. Used for incident, compliance, and operational forensics. Pagination required. Each actor filter uses UUID per corresponding entity table.

id.description: Unique identifier for the audit log record. The immutable primary key in shopping_audit_logs table. Used for reference and traceability in all compliance/audit tasks and reporting.

oneOf.description: UUID of the admin actor who performed the operation. Nullable—if the operation was not performed by an admin, this field is null. For example, operations done by sellers or automated systems will have null.

admin_id.description: UUID of the admin actor who performed the operation (nullable). Refers to shopping_admins.id. Used in security, compliance, or traceability contexts for privileged operations. If the event was performed by a seller, customer, or automated process, this will be null. Enables cross-relating actions and actors during incident investigations.

oneOf.description: UUID of the seller actor affected by this operation. Nullable—present if the operation concerns a seller (e.g., account suspension, refund approval). Null otherwise. Used for investigation, filtering, or reporting by business relationship.

seller_id.description: UUID of the seller actor affected by this audit log event (nullable). Corresponds to shopping_sellers.id. Included for incidents that affect a seller's account, actions, or data. Supports context-aware incident response and role-based filtering. Null if unrelated to a seller.

oneOf.description: UUID of the customer actor affected by this operation. Nullable—present if the operation concerns a customer (e.g., order refund, privilege escalation). Null otherwise. Used for compliance, privacy, or individual trace queries.

customer_id.description: UUID of the customer actor affected (nullable). Maps to shopping_customers.id. Used to trace audit events in compliance reviews, incident analysis, or privacy investigations. Null when event is not related to any customer actor.

category.description: Structured log category or domain (e.g., 'security', 'order', 'refund', 'inventory'). Specifies the high-level business area the event pertains to, guiding admin focus during investigations or audits. Common values map to logical system domains for analytics and compliance.

event_type.description: Machine-readable event type code for the specific action (e.g., 'ADMIN_SUSPEND_SELLER', 'ORDER_MANUAL_REFUND', 'PRIV_ESCALATION'). Used for fine-grained filtering, analytics, security event correlation, or policy enforcement. Maps directly to event_type column in audit log schema.

oneOf.description: IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) from which this operation originated. Null if not recorded or non-attributable. Useful for trace and forensics in case of incidents involving fraud or administrative access.

ip.description: Origin IP address (nullable). Indicates the source of an operation, supporting security log correlation and investigation. Null if unavailable or not applicable to the event.

oneOf.description: Optional human-readable description of the business or security event for reporting or investigation. Can be null if not explicitly specified by the system; typical use includes comments by actors, system-generated summaries, or workflow documentation.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the audit log record (nullable). Used to supply business context, comments, or highlights useful for audits, moderation review, or legal traceability. May be absent for system-generated records or low-context audit events.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the audit event was created. Record creation is atomic and immutable. Enables chronological search and sequence analysis in forensics reviews and detailed audit trails.

IShoppingAuditLog.ISummary.description: Summary representation of an audit log record. Used for listing and quick reference of audit events related to admin, seller, or customer operations. Derived from shopping_audit_logs and required for all compliance, security, and operational investigations. Each field provides trace, actor, and contextual metadata to enable full-lifecycle event tracking and business reporting, with enriched property descriptions for admin-end user clarity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the audit log event record, corresponding to the 'id' column in shopping_audit_logs. This serves as the primary key for referencing and querying specific audit events. Example: '23ebfc9d-ec7c-410a-b4ef-44250f66fd41'.

admin_id.description: Optional reference to the admin actor who performed the logged operation. Corresponds to 'admin_id' in shopping_audit_logs; nullable if the audit log event was not triggered by an admin actor.

seller_id.description: Optional seller account affected by this audit action, as referenced by 'seller_id'. Nullable in case the event is not linked to a specific seller.

customer_id.description: Optional customer account affected by or participating in this audit event. Sourced from 'customer_id'; nullable if not actor- or customer-focused.

category.description: Structured log category/domain string, mapping to the 'category' column (e.g., 'security', 'order', 'refund'). Used for filtering and classifying audit activities.

event_type.description: Constant representing the specific nature of the event (e.g., 'ADMIN_SUSPEND_SELLER', 'ORDER_MANUAL_REFUND'). Corresponds to the 'event_type' column in shopping_audit_logs.

ip.description: IP address from which the operation originated, for traceability and investigation. Sourced from 'ip'; nullable as not all events may have an associated IP.

description.description: A human-readable summary of the business event, for investigative auditing or reporting. Matches the 'description' column; may be null if not supplied for the event.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the audit event record was created. Sourced from the 'created_at' column; expressed in ISO 8601 format. Example: '2025-10-31T13:51:55.262Z'.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last update to this audit log record (immutable but may indicate annotation). Maps from 'updated_at'; ISO 8601 UTC.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete marker for removal from default query/reporting views. Corresponds to 'deleted_at'; nullable—null indicates an active, visible log entry.

IShoppingAuditLog.description: Detailed single-event audit log record representing critical business/security operation. Maps to a row in the shopping_audit_logs table, including actor (admin, seller, customer) references, event type/category, summary, IP, and audit timestamps. Used for platform compliance, regulatory reviews, and investigative reporting.

status.description: Status of announcements to filter for. Example: 'draft', 'active', 'expired', or 'scheduled'. If not specified, returns all statuses allowed by actor's role.

target_audience.description: Audience segment/role to search for. Permitted values: 'all', 'customers', 'sellers', 'admins'. If omitted, includes all matching announcements.

publish_start_after.description: Start of publish window (filter only announcements scheduled to publish after this datetime, ISO 8601). Optional.

publish_end_before.description: End of publish window (filter only announcements scheduled to end before this datetime, ISO 8601). Optional.

search.description: Full-text keyword to search over title and body of announcements via similarity, supporting dash-board level search and reporting. Optional.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Optional; default is 1 if not provided.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page (default per business rule; maximum 100 as per requirements).

sort_by.description: Sort field name; permitted values include 'created_at', 'publish_start_at', 'publish_end_at', 'title'. Optional.

oneOf.description: Sort direction; only valid values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Optional.
Sort direction; only valid values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Optional.

order.description: Sort direction; only valid values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Optional.

IShoppingPlatformAnnouncement.IRequest.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria for querying platform announcements (shopping_platform_announcements). Includes status, audience, publication window, keyword search, and standard pagination/sorting fields. Used as request body for dashboard/admin portal/search features.

id.description: Unique identifier for the platform announcement. This is the primary key in the shopping_platform_announcements table.

admin_id.description: Reference to the admin (shopping_admins) who authored this platform announcement. Used for audit and traceability.

title.description: Title of the platform announcement. Used in notification headers and announcement listings.

body.description: Full content of the platform announcement, may support markdown formatting.

target_audience.description: Audience segment/role for this announcement: e.g., 'all', 'customers', 'sellers', 'admins'. Controls which users receive or see this notice.

status.description: Current lifecycle status for the announcement: e.g., 'draft', 'scheduled', 'active', 'expired', 'hidden'. Used to manage visibility.

publish_start_at.description: Scheduled start date/time for announcement visibility. Null if unscheduled.

publish_end_at.description: Optional scheduled end date/time after which this announcement should be hidden from display. Null if indefinite.

created_at.description: Datetime the announcement was initially created.

updated_at.description: Datetime of most recent update to announcement content or state.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp, or null if not deleted.

IShoppingPlatformAnnouncement.description: Represents a single platform-wide announcement authored by an administrator. Used for global notifications, compliance, maintenance notices, or other communication targeting users with configurable visibility windows. Based on the shopping_platform_announcements table. All activity is audited via admin_id, and records are soft-deletable to comply with regulatory retention standards.

title.description: Announcement title. Required when creating new announcements. Should be unique among active announcements. Used in system notifications, user dashboards, and compliance communications.

body.description: The full text/content of the announcement. May support markdown formatting and is required for all announcements. This message constitutes the primary body visible to users based on their role and the targeting strategy.

target_audience.description: Audience segment for this announcement (e.g., 'all', 'customers', 'sellers', 'admins'). Controls which user types will see the announcement: set to 'all' for platform-wide, or specify a targeted user group. Only values in the allowed enum are accepted.

status.description: Initial workflow status after creation. Must be one of: 'draft' (not yet published), 'scheduled' (pending a future activation), 'active' (immediately live for eligible audience), or 'hidden' (manually hidden or unpublished). Controls announcement lifecycle and determines visibility logic for the user interfaces and API clients.

oneOf.description: Scheduled UTC datetime for when this announcement will first become visible. Required only if status is 'scheduled'; must be in the future. Omit or set to null for 'draft' or immediate 'active' status.

publish_start_at.description: Scheduled UTC datetime for announcement visibility window start. Required only if status is 'scheduled'; may be omitted/null otherwise. Must be future-dated; ensures compliance with business policy on scheduled releases.

oneOf.description: UTC datetime for when the announcement should be hidden or considered expired. May be null for indefinite announcements. For scheduled/active announcements, set to indicate expiration; for drafts or hidden, leave null.

publish_end_at.description: UTC datetime for hiding/expiring the announcement. If null, announcement remains visible until manually hidden. This field is relevant for 'scheduled' or 'active' statuses and ignored for 'draft' or 'hidden'.

IShoppingPlatformAnnouncement.ICreate.description: DTO for creation of a platform announcement by an admin. Includes all fields controllable at authoring (title, body, target audience, workflow status, and publication window). admin_id is system-assigned and state transitions/audit are backend managed. Follows shopping_platform_announcements table and the admin-only POST /shopping/admin/platformAnnouncements operation. See business requirements for usage: use 'draft' to save, 'scheduled' with publish_start_at for timed future releases, 'active' for immediate display, and 'hidden' to unpublish/expire before publish_end_at. All fields must comply with business logic and allowed state transitions.

title.description: Updated announcement title for ongoing communication, notifications, and listing screens. Must remain unique among all active announcements. Should concisely reflect maintenance, legal, or business message.

body.description: Full text/content of the announcement. May be updated for clarity or extended per event. Markdown formatting is allowed.

target_audience.description: Updated audience for this announcement (must be one of: 'all', 'customers', 'sellers', 'admins'). Controls real-time visibility, user targeting, and compliance notification. Only valid values are permitted for status update or targeting change.

status.description: Lifecycle status for the announcement. Allowed transitions: 'draft'→'scheduled', 'scheduled'↔'active', 'active'→'expired'/'hidden', 'draft'/'active'/'scheduled'↔'hidden'. Must use: 'draft', 'scheduled', 'active', 'expired', or 'hidden'. A transition to 'scheduled' requires a future-dated publish_start_at; setting status to 'active' means immediate visibility to the audience.

publish_start_at.description: Datetime when the announcement is scheduled for visibility (ISO 8601 format). Required and must be future-dated if moving to 'scheduled' status; can be null (omitted) if moving to 'draft', 'active' (immediate), or 'hidden'/expired state.

publish_end_at.description: Datetime when announcement should become hidden (expired/hidden states). Null for open-ended announcements that should remain visible until manually hidden. If status is set to 'expired'/'hidden', this field should match the deactivation/expiration time.

IShoppingPlatformAnnouncement.IUpdate.description: Details for updating a platform announcement. Used by admin to edit the title, body, status, target audience, and publication window dates. This type maps to the 'shopping_platform_announcements' table for PUT /shopping/admin/platformAnnouncements/{platformAnnouncementId}. Only enum values for status are permitted ('draft', 'scheduled', 'active', 'expired', 'hidden'). A scheduled status requires a future publish_start_at; active is immediate unless overridden. Audit logs track all edits, and date values must conform to ISO 8601. For retiring/expiring an announcement, set status to 'hidden' or 'expired', and optionally update publish_end_at. All field transitions are subject to business rule validation.

action_type.description: Filter results by admin action type (e.g., 'GRANT_ROLE', 'FORCE_RESET', 'SUSPEND_SELLER', etc.). Optional.

entity_type.description: Filter logs by affected entity type (e.g., 'product', 'order', 'user', 'setting'). Optional.

entity_id.description: Filter logs by specific target entity UUID (if searching for actions on a given entity). Optional.

admin_id.description: Filter logs by the acting admin's user ID (search by admin actor). Optional.

affected_admin_id.description: Filter logs by the target/affected admin (if relevant). Optional.

affected_seller_id.description: Filter logs by the target/affected seller (if relevant). Optional.

affected_customer_id.description: Filter logs by the affected customer (if relevant). Optional.

reason.description: Free-text search within the business context or rationale for admin action. Optional.

created_at_from.description: Filter for admin action logs created on or after this datetime (inclusive). Optional, ISO8601.

created_at_to.description: Filter for admin action logs created on or before this datetime (inclusive). Optional, ISO8601.

page.description: Page number for paginated results (1-based offset). Optional.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page (default value is 20, optional, should not exceed 100).

sort_by.description: Sort order for results, e.g., 'created_at', 'admin_id', 'entity_type'. Optional.

oneOf.description: Sort direction: ascending or descending. Optional.
Sort direction: ascending or descending. Optional.

sort_order.description: Sort direction: ascending or descending. Optional.

IShoppingAdminActionLog.IRequest.description: Parameters for filtering and searching admin action logs in the shopping_admin_action_logs table. Supports action type, entity, actor/affected parties, full-text reason search, time range, paging, and sort order for audit/compliance use cases. All filters are optional. Pagination parameters (page, limit) and sorting controls (sort_by, sort_order) are included for large data sets.

IShoppingAdminActionLog.description: Represents a single admin action log entry for audit and compliance, mapped from the shopping_admin_action_logs table. Captures each critical operation taken by an admin actor on the platform, including privilege escalations, data changes, suspensions, and policy enforcement. Contains references to the acting admin, affected admin, seller, or customer (when relevant), the nature/type of the action performed (e.g., GRANT_ROLE, FORCE_RESET, SUSPEND_SELLER), optional business/context rationale, the target entity if applicable, timestamps for event and record creation, and soft deletion marker. This entity forms the basis of the system's immutable, auditable event history for regulatory reviews and operational investigations. Each log entry is immutable and can be used for tracing the full lifecycle of privileged operations.

id.description: Primary key and unique identifier for the admin action log entry.

oneOf.description: Acting admin's unique identifier (nullable if performed by system or unknown context). FK to shopping_admins.id.

admin_id.description: Acting admin's unique identifier (nullable if performed by system or unknown context). FK to shopping_admins.id.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the affected admin account if this operation targeted another admin. Nullable.

affected_admin_id.description: Identifier of the affected admin account if this operation targeted another admin. Nullable.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the affected seller account (nullable if not relevant).

affected_seller_id.description: Identifier of the affected seller account (nullable if not relevant).

oneOf.description: Customer account affected by this action, if relevant. Nullable.

affected_customer_id.description: Customer account affected by this action, if relevant. Nullable.

action_type.description: Constant representing the type of admin operation performed (e.g., GRANT_ROLE, FORCE_RESET, SUSPEND_SELLER).

oneOf.description: Type of entity affected by this action log (e.g., product, order, user, setting). Nullable.

entity_type.description: Type of entity affected by this action log (e.g., product, order, user, setting). Nullable.

oneOf.description: UUID of entity affected by this action, if applicable (e.g., product, order, user).

entity_id.description: UUID of entity affected by this action, if applicable (e.g., product, order, user).
